The Big Picture: What Robotics Research in 2025 Is Really Trying To Do

*A plain-words read of both big robotics meetings of 2025 together — ICRA (1,604 papers) and IROS (1,985 papers), about 3,589 papers in all.*

1. The one problem

Strip away the details and every robot is trying to do one thing: act in the real world on its own, without a person steering it the whole time. You tell it what you want ("clear the table," "drive me home," "put the needle here," "fly down this pipe and check it"), and it has to work out the rest by itself and get it right.

That is hard for one reason: the real world does not hold still and does not tell you what is in it. A robot cannot see everything. Light changes, weather changes, things move, some things are see-through or shiny, water is murky, and the robot only gets a noisy, partial picture through its cameras and sensors. On top of that, touching things is messy — when a hand grips an object or a needle presses on tissue, the forces are hard to guess ahead of time. And whatever the robot decides to do, it has to do it *now*, using the small, cheap computer bolted onto its body, not a giant server farm somewhere else.

So the one problem is: take in an unclear, changing picture of the world, decide what to do, and move a physical body to do it — reliably, quickly, safely, and cheaply. Both meetings, and nearly all 3,589 papers, are chipping away at some piece of that. The two meetings do not disagree about the problem. They split the work up in almost the same way. Where they differ is in how much weight they put on each piece, and I will point that out as we go.

2. The loop everything hangs on

Underneath all the work is the same three-step loop, running over and over, many times a second:

1. Sense — take in what is around the robot (cameras, radar, laser scanners, touch, distance sensors) and turn it into something the robot can reason about.

2. Decide — work out what to do next, from the big plan ("first pick up the cup") down to the fine motion ("move the hand two centimeters left").

3. Move — send commands to the motors so the body actually does it.

Then it senses again to check what happened, and repeats. Most of robotics is making one of those three steps better.

Four hard rules cut across *all* of the work, no matter which step, and both meetings name them again and again:

  • It has to run fast on a small computer. The robot carries its own brain. Being right is not enough if the answer comes too late to use. "Right but too slow or too costly to run live" is the single most common complaint in the papers at both meetings — one of the top IROS papers is simply a laser-scan mapping method redone so it does not need a heavy graphics chip at all.
  • It has to learn without needing millions of examples. Teaching a robot by showing it examples works, but collecting those examples on real hardware is slow and expensive, so a lot of effort goes into needing fewer of them, or making fake ones.
  • It must not hurt people. Robots move real mass around real humans. A wrong move can injure someone, so a lot of work goes into keeping the robot inside safe limits.
  • It should work on more than one robot or job. Research wants methods that carry over — one skill that works on several robots, or in places the robot has never seen — instead of hand-tuning everything from scratch each time.

Keep those three steps and four rules in mind. Every theme below is just a different attack on them.

3. How the field breaks the problem down

Group A — Seeing the world and building a picture of it (the "sense" step)

This is the biggest chunk of work at both meetings by a clear margin. At ICRA, seeing-related work (perception) covers 644 papers; at IROS it covers 817 — the single largest tag at either meeting. Three ideas dominate.

Cheap, fast, reliable seeing. The robot has to understand what it is looking at accurately *and* fast enough to run on its own small computer, even in hard cases — see-through glass, bad weather, long distance, small far-away objects, moving scenes. The fixes are slimming down vision programs so they use less computing, and mixing several sensors so that when one fails another covers for it (for example, camera plus radar). At ICRA, *Lightstereo* judges distance from two side-by-side cameras with far less computing than usual, and *Unleashing HyDRa* fuses radar with cameras so 3D vision holds up at long range and in bad light. At IROS, the standout is *UAV-DETR*, a spot-things program tuned to find small objects in pictures taken from flying drones — by far the most-cited paper at either meeting.

One shared way to store the 3D world. Many jobs — mapping a room, rebuilding a scene, tracking where the robot is while it maps (SLAM) — each used to need their own way to store what the world looks like in 3D. A newer method builds a scene out of many tiny colored blobs of light that are fast to draw and look realistic (Gaussian Splatting), and papers at both meetings reuse it as one common format. IROS leans especially hard on making this method small and quick: its top perception papers are about squeezing the blob-maps down so they fit in memory and run live (*CGS-SLAM*), and about doing dynamic mapping with no heavy graphics chip at all (*NGD-SLAM*).

Self-driving cars, done leaner and safer. Full self-driving systems that build a heavy top-down picture of everything around the car cost too much computing and can still make unsafe plans. The fix is to describe only the parts that matter, tie seeing and planning together more tightly, and have the car track how unsure it is. ICRA's most-cited paper of all, *SparseDrive*, does exactly this. Both meetings carry a large driving load (247 papers at ICRA, 277 at IROS).

Group B — Understanding goals and deciding what to do (the "decide" step)

People give robots open-ended goals in plain words, but older planners could not handle that flexibility. The big move at both meetings is to use the same kind of AI that powers chatbots (large language models) to break a spoken goal into an ordered list of robot steps — but *not* to trust that AI blindly. The plan is written in a strict, checkable form and each step is tested to make sure it is physically doable. ICRA's *Guiding Long-Horizon Task and Motion Planning with Vision Language Models* pairs a language model with a classic planner that checks each move is possible.

A second, closely tied line turns "seeing and talking" AI into "doing" AI: retrain the model so its output is robot movements, not just words (vision-language-action models), and sharpen its weak sense of depth and 3D space. Both meetings put heavy weight here (foundation-model work: 251 papers at ICRA, 307 at IROS). This is one place the two differ in flavor. IROS pushes these language-driven robots into concrete jobs faster — a robot scrub nurse that hands over surgical tools (*RoboNurse-VLA*), a proactive office assistant (*AssistantX*), a drone guided by spoken directions outdoors (*KiteRunner*). And IROS's most-cited planning paper, *Safety Aware Task Planning via Large Language Models*, is specifically about the fact that these language planners chase finishing the job and ignore safety — a worry ICRA raises too but IROS puts front and center.

A third line is getting several robots to work together, which is much harder than one robot. Both meetings carry a large team-robot load (169 papers at ICRA, 194 at IROS), with IROS leaning toward flying swarms — many drones holding formation while dodging obstacles.

Group C — Moving the body well (the "move" step)

Teaching legs and humanoids to move. Legged and human-shaped robots need to walk, balance, and use their hands without an engineer hand-designing a target for every task, and a skill learned inside a computer often fails on the real machine. The fixes are training in a computer copy of the world and getting it to still work on the real robot (sim-to-real), building one flexible controller for many tasks, and giving the robot an inner guess of what it will feel next. ICRA's *HOVER* is one controller that runs many whole-body tasks on a humanoid; its *Berkeley Humanoid* is a cheap open human-shaped robot built for smooth transfer to real hardware. IROS goes more toward the mechanical and energy side — an energy-thrifty walker that reuses its own swing (*The Duke Humanoid*), a four-legged robot that climbs ladders, and a careful study of how joint friction is the hidden reason computer-trained walkers fail on real ground.

Planning motion in real time. Working out the best possible way to move a complex body, moment by moment, is too slow to do exactly. The fix is to try many possible short-future motions, score them, and blend the good ones (sampling-based control), and to learn a rough model of how the body responds. Both meetings carry this heavily (mpc: 103 papers at ICRA, 114 at IROS).

Handling things by feel, not just by looking. Controllers that only track position fail whenever force matters — pushing a peg into a hole, peeling a vegetable, wiping, fitting parts. The fix is to make force and touch signals the controller reads and manages directly, and let the robot choose how firm or gentle to be (compliance). ICRA's most-cited manipulation paper, *Learning Visuotactile Skills With Two Multifingered Hands*, does two-handed fine work by feel. IROS's manipulation work tilts toward getting the teaching examples in the first place — its top manipulation paper, *Bunny-VisionPro*, is a rig for a person to puppet two dexterous hands in real time — and toward cheaper hands, like the open low-cost *ORCA* hand.

One flexible tool for both seeing and acting. Robots often face several equally good options at once, and simple methods either freeze or pick a shaky average. A method first built to make images — start from random noise, clean it up into a good result (diffusion) — is pointed instead at making robot movements, because it keeps many good options apart cleanly. Both meetings use it about equally (roughly 72 papers each), with IROS favoring versions that read 3D directly and run faster (*3D Diffusion Policies*, *Mamba Policy*).

Group D — The cross-cutting rules: data, safety, cost, and hard real-world jobs

Making training examples cheaper is the field's real bottleneck at both meetings — better ways to record a person doing a task (through see-through headset gear and head-worn cameras), automatic ways to make many examples from a few, and turning fake computer-made data into training fuel. IROS adds a strong "just make it in the computer" streak: large fake-data generators for seeing (*Synthetica*) and a pipeline that scans real objects into computer copies by picking them up (*Scalable Real2Sim*).

Safety and being sure it won't fail grows more urgent as learned and chatbot-style parts enter the control loop. Both meetings use math guardrails that block any command crossing a safety line (control barrier functions), plan-checkers, and — at ICRA — deliberately trying to trick a language-model robot into harmful acts (*Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots*). The counts are close (159 at ICRA, 164 at IROS), but the angle differs: ICRA exposes the danger; IROS leans toward building safety into the planner and handling risk in crowds and faults.

The same methods pushed into hard real jobs — medicine, flying, underwater, outdoor field work — each break the standard tools with their own troubles. This is the sharpest split between the two meetings. IROS is markedly more physical-world and medical: soft, bendable robots (223 papers vs. ICRA's 131) and medical robots (219 vs. 121) are far larger there, with steerable drilling robots for bone, growing "vine" robots that snake into the spine, and surgical soft-tissue simulators. ICRA carries these too but with lighter weight.

Soft and body-inspired machines round out the picture: bendable parts that change how stiff they are, cable-pulled arms, muscle-like actuators, designs copied from living creatures — a body that can flex reaches and touches safely where a rigid one cannot.

4. The whole picture in one paragraph

Put both meetings together and they are one effort: build robots that can take in an unclear, changing world, decide what to do about it, and move a real body to do it — fast enough for a small onboard computer, learned from as few examples as possible, safe around people, and general enough to carry to new robots and new jobs. The seeing themes make the picture clearer and cheaper; the deciding themes turn plain-language goals into checked, doable plans, alone or in teams; the moving themes make bodies act well by feel and in real time; and the cross-cutting themes fight the real limits — the cost of training data, the need for safety, and the demands of hard settings. The two meetings agree on all of this. ICRA tilts a little more toward the newest AI-brain ideas and toward naming the dangers (it holds the biggest headline citation counts on self-driving and touch, and the sharpest safety warning). IROS tilts more toward the body and the world — flying, medicine, soft machines, energy, and making the computer generate its own data — and it puts the "make the plan safe, and make it run on cheap hardware" worry even more front and center. Two big things are still not solved at either meeting. First, many of the best methods are accurate but too slow or too costly to run live on the robot's own computer — "right but too late" is the most common problem the papers name. Second, the work on being able to *promise* a robot won't fail is falling behind how fast these learned and language-driven systems are being put to work.

The two forces underneath everything

Two forces shape almost everything at both conferences: the fight to run methods cheaply, and the fight to get enough data to train them. They are really one story — the field has powerful methods that are heavy to run and hungry for examples, and most of 2025's work is about making them light enough to run and cheap enough to feed.

Seeing is the biggest job, and the fight is cost

More papers are about seeing — making sense of the camera and sensor feed — than about anything else. But the hard part is not accuracy, it is cost. About 985 of the 3,589 papers (~27%) frame their main problem around speed or compute: this works, but it is too slow or too heavy to run live on the robot's own computer. That is the most common single complaint in the whole set, and it is slightly louder at IROS (535) than ICRA (450).

The reason is physical: the robot carries its own small computer. An answer that comes a second too late, or that needs a server-grade graphics card, is useless in a live control loop. So a large share of the best work is not a new idea — it is taking a good-but-heavy method and making it light enough to actually use:

  • Lightstereo (ICRA) — judging distance from two cameras normally needs a giant 4D data structure that is too slow for real time; they get the same accuracy from a much lighter version.
  • CGS-SLAM (IROS) — building a 3D map out of millions of little blobs uses too much memory and runs too slow; they compress it to a compact set.
  • Full-order sampling MPC (ICRA) — computing exact joint torques for walking is too slow, and the usual fast shortcut is too rough; they find a middle path that is both fast and good.
  • HOVER (ICRA) — instead of a separate controller for walking, carrying, and tabletop work, one controller does all of them, so there is less to compute and maintain.

The pattern is compress, prune, simplify, unify. The methods already work; the job is making them affordable to run.

Underneath, the real bottleneck is data

Cost has a twin, and it is data. About 485 papers (~13%) frame their problem around it directly, and the two are the same story from different angles: the powerful learning methods work if you feed them enough examples, and examples are slow and expensive to collect on real hardware. The binding constraint is not the method anymore; it is the supply of data. The field attacks that from three sides:

1. Record people better — capture what ordinary demonstrations miss. ForceMimic (ICRA) records the forces a person applies while peeling a vegetable, not just where the hand moved, because contact tasks fail without that. Bunny-VisionPro (IROS) is a real-time two-handed teleoperation rig built to collect clean two-arm demonstrations.

2. Multiply a few examples automatically — take a handful of real demonstrations and generate thousands of valid variations, so one afternoon of human effort stretches much further.

3. Make fake data inside a computer — especially at IROS. The catch is that simulated images look wrong, so a policy trained on them fails on the real robot; SplatSim (ICRA) fixes that by using the blob-based 3D method (Gaussian splatting) to make simulated images look real enough that the skill transfers.

The blunt takeaway the field is acting on: cheap examples matter more than clever methods right now. If you can make data cheaply — record it better, multiply it, or fake it convincingly — you win, because the methods are already good enough once they are fed.

The two forces are one story

2025 robotics has capable methods that are hungry (need lots of data) and heavy (need lots of compute). Almost none of the headline effort is inventing a brand-new kind of robot brain. It is making the brains we already have cheap enough to feed and light enough to run. That is the real shape of the field this year: affordability and integration over invention.

How the field breaks the problem down — every theme, every paper

Sense — see the world

Cheap, fast, reliable seeing 21 papers

The problem

The robot has to understand what it is looking at accurately and fast enough to run on its own small computer, even in hard cases like see-through glass, bad weather, long distances, small far-away objects, and moving scenes.

The approaches

Slim down vision programs so they use less computing, and mix several sensors together, for example a camera plus radar, so that when one sensor fails another covers for it. Some read distance from two side-by-side cameras more cheaply, some spot tiny objects in pictures taken from flying drones, and some handle see-through objects.

How it solves it

Trimming the computing keeps it fast enough for the onboard computer, and combining sensors fills the gaps where any single sensor is weak.

all 21 papers
IROS6cNeuFlow-V2: Push High-Efficiency Optical Flow To the LimitMeasuring motion between video frames is either accurate or fast, but not both on cheap robot hardware.
ICRA3cEstimating User Engagement in Human Robot Interaction Using a Dynamic Bayesian NetworkFiguring out whether a person talking to a robot is genuinely engaged is hard because the relevant signals — eye contact, head position, facial expression, body heat — come from different sensors and shift over time.
IROS3cYO-CSA-T: A Real-time Badminton Tracking System Utilizing YOLO Based on Contextual and Spatial AttentionTracking a fast shuttlecock in real time is hard because it moves so fast it blurs and blends into the court lines.
ICRA2cUnified Human Localization and Trajectory Prediction with Monocular Vision ↗Predicting where a person will walk next using only one ordinary camera requires first knowing exactly where they are in the real world, and current prediction models break down when that position estimate is noisy.
ICRA2cmmDEAR: mmWave Point Cloud Density Enhancement for Accurate Human Body ReconstructionRadar sensors that work through walls give only a very sparse scatter of points, which is not enough to reconstruct the shape and pose of a human body.
IROS1cContext-aware Sparse Spatiotemporal Learning for Event-based VisionNeuromorphic chips give spiking vision networks high sparsity but low accuracy, while deep learning gets accuracy but wastes power and can't run on neuromorphic chips.
ICRADepth Estimation Through Translucent SurfacesDepth sensors and stereo cameras cannot measure distance through or behind translucent materials because the mixed light signals confuse them.
ICRASeeing Eye to Eye: Design and Evaluation of a Custom Expressive Eye Display Module for the Stretch Mobile ManipulatorMobile robots have no good way to signal to nearby people where they are looking or what state they are in, making it hard for people to work alongside them.
ICRARobotic 3D Flower Pose Estimation for Small-Scale Urban Farms ↗A robot that pollinates strawberry plants needs to know exactly where each small flower is and which way it faces, which is hard from raw 3D sensor data.
ICRAA Unified End-to-End Network for Category-Level and Instance-Level Object Pose Estimation from RGB ImagesFiguring out the exact position and orientation of an object from a plain color photo — with no depth sensor — is hard, and most methods work for either a specific object or a category of objects, not both.
ICRAA Cane-Mounted System for Dynamic Orientation Prediction for Correcting Incorrect Cane-Tapping by Visually Challenged PersonsVisually impaired people often hold their guide cane at the wrong angle, which reduces how well it detects obstacles, but there is no way to automatically detect and correct this in real time.
IROSRGBTrack: Fast, Robust Depth-Free 6D Pose Estimation and TrackingTracking the exact position and orientation of an object in real time under fast movement and partial blocking normally requires a depth camera, which is not always available.
IROSOne-Shot Gesture Recognition for Underwater Diver-To-Robot Communication*Getting an underwater robot to reliably recognize a diver's hand gestures is hard because the water is murky, lighting is poor, and training a deep learning model needs many labeled examples plus retraining for each new gesture.
IROSLearning-based Keypoints Detection with Topological Order on Deformable Linear Objects from Incomplete Point CloudsFinding key locations along flexible objects like cables from a 3D scan is unreliable because scans are often incomplete and the points must stay in the correct order along the cable.
IROSRobot-Mediated gesture-based memory game for older adult psychophysical stimulationBrain and body exercise games for older people use touchscreens and don't combine memory work with arm movements.
IROS3-D Multiple Sound Source Localization Based on a Five-Element Microphone ArrayFinding where multiple people or sounds are located in 3D space with cheap equipment and fast computation is hard when sounds are all mixed together and you want to use only a few microphones.
IROSCorrespondence-Free Pose Estimation with Patterns: A Unified Approach for Multi-Dimensional VisionFinding the position and rotation of an object usually requires matching specific points on the object to a model, but this breaks down with new objects and when the view angle is not standard 3D-to-2D projection.
IROSImproved Calibration for Panoramic Annular Lens Systems with Angular ModulationStandard camera math does not work for panoramic ring cameras because their unusual design compresses the view in ways standard formulas do not capture.
IROSRCGNet: RGB-based Category-Level 6D Object Pose Estimation with Geometric GuidanceRobots can't know an object's position and rotation from regular camera photos alone when they don't have depth sensors.
IROSAction Recognition for Underwater Gesture Communication in Human Diver and Robot TeamingUnderwater cameras blur hand signs because water moves light around, and shadows block parts of the motion.
IROSComplete Corruption-Aware Retinex Framework for Low-Light Image EnhancementMaking dark images brighter creates extra noise and blurry spots that the enhancement itself introduced, not just from the camera, so existing fix-up methods only deal with half the problem.

One shared way to store the 3D world 447 papers

The problem

Many jobs, such as mapping a room, rebuilding a scene, or tracking where the robot is while it maps, each needed their own way to store what the world looks like in 3D, which is wasteful, heavy on memory, and hard to connect together.

The approaches

A newer method builds a 3D scene out of many tiny colored blobs of light that are fast to draw and look realistic (Gaussian Splatting). Papers use it as one common format for mapping and for tracking the robot's place, and push hard to shrink it so it fits in memory and runs live, even without a heavy graphics chip.

How it solves it

One shared format lets the seeing side and the deciding side speak the same language, so a scene captured once can be reused for mapping, planning, or training, and the shrinking work keeps it fast enough for the robot.

all 447 papers
ICRA16cRobo-GS: A Physics Consistent Spatial-Temporal Model for Robotic Arm with Hybrid RepresentationBuilding a simulation replica of a real robot arm that looks right, has accurate geometry, and behaves physically correctly all at the same time is not possible with any single existing representation.
ICRA12cBeyond Bare Queries: Open-Vocabulary Object Grounding with 3D Scene GraphWhen you ask a robot to find an object using a description that involves other nearby objects (like 'the cup to the left of the red bowl'), current systems fail because they cannot reason about spatial relationships.
ICRA12cSplatSim: Zero-Shot Sim2Real Transfer of RGB Manipulation Policies Using Gaussian SplattingManipulation policies trained in simulation using synthetic images fail when placed on a real robot because the simulated images look different from real camera images.
IROS12cCGS-SLAM: Compact 3D Gaussian Splatting for Dense Visual SLAMSystems that build 3D maps using many small floating blobs (3D Gaussian Splatting) use too much memory and are too slow because they keep millions of redundant blobs.
ICRA11cGARAD-SLAM: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Anti Dynamic SLAMWhen a robot maps and tracks its position in a scene using 3D Gaussian Splatting, moving people or objects corrupt the map and cause the location estimate to drift.
ICRA11cGaussianRoom: Improving 3D Gaussian Splatting with SDF Guidance and Monocular Cues for Indoor Scene ReconstructionReconstructing indoor rooms with many plain, textureless walls using 3D Gaussian Splatting produces incomplete or noisy results because the initial point placement is poor and the optimization has nothing to anchor to in featureless areas.
ICRA10cSeaSplat: Representing Underwater Scenes with 3D Gaussian Splatting and a Physically Grounded Image Formation ModelUnderwater images look hazy and color-shifted because light scatters and absorbs differently at different depths and wavelengths, which makes 3D scene reconstruction from those images inaccurate.
ICRA9cDigiforests: a Longitudinal Lidar Dataset for Forestry Robotics ↗Robots working in forests need to identify trees and measure their growth over time, but no dataset with repeated scans and detailed per-tree labels existed to develop or test such abilities.
ICRA8cReMEmbR: Building and Reasoning Over Long-Horizon Spatio-Temporal Memory for Robot NavigationA robot operating over hours or days cannot quickly answer questions like "where did you last see the red cup?" because it has no structured way to store and search its past observations.
ICRA8cKinematic-ICP: Enhancing LiDAR Odometry with Kinematic Constraints for Wheeled Mobile Robots Moving on Planar SurfacesA wheeled robot estimating its position from laser scans drifts over time because the scan-matching step ignores the fact that the robot can only move along the ground.
ICRA8cMapEx: Indoor Structure Exploration with Probabilistic Information Gain from Global Map PredictionsRobots exploring buildings take inefficient paths because they only look at the edge of what they have seen, without using the fact that buildings follow predictable patterns like rectangular rooms and straight corridors.
ICRA8cKISS-Matcher: Fast and Robust Point Cloud Registration RevisitedAligning two 3D point clouds is slow because filtering out wrong point matches takes a lot of computation, and no single open-source tool covers the full process.
ICRA8cSPINE: Online Semantic Planning for Missions with Incomplete Natural Language Specifications in Unstructured EnvironmentsRobots sent on missions described in plain language often get incomplete instructions and must still navigate unmapped places while understanding what different things in the environment mean.
ICRA8cRGB-Only Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Unbounded Outdoor Scenes ↗Existing systems that build a 3D scene map and track camera position at the same time require a depth sensor or a pre-trained depth model and fall apart in large outdoor spaces.
ICRA8cLarge-Scale UWB Anchor Calibration and One-Shot Localization Using Gaussian ProcessSetting up the radio beacons (UWB anchors) used for indoor positioning in huge spaces like seaports takes a long time, and walls often block the signal so distance readings are unreliable.
IROS8cNGD-SLAM: Towards Real-Time Dynamic SLAM without GPUMaking a real-time map while a robot moves in a changing scene is slow when you use artificial intelligence to ignore moving objects, because it needs a powerful GPU and the camera gets stuck waiting for the masking to finish.
IROS8cSemGauss-SLAM: Dense Semantic Gaussian Splatting SLAMMapping systems that build 3D models as the robot moves don't understand what the objects are (semantics), and adding semantics usually breaks the tracking and rendering.
ICRA7cRealm: Real-Time Line-of-Sight Maintenance in Multi-Robot Navigation with Unknown ObstaclesA group of robots exploring an unknown space can lose direct visibility to each other behind unexpected obstacles, breaking communication links.
ICRA7cGaussian-LIC: Real-Time Photo-Realistic SLAM with Gaussian Splatting and LiDAR-Inertial-Camera FusionSystems that build photo-realistic maps of a space while navigating only work indoors with depth cameras and fail outside or when the robot moves quickly.
ICRA7cLiftFeat: 3D Geometry-Aware Local Feature MatchingSmall, fast image-matching networks break down when lighting changes sharply or when surfaces look the same across a wide area, which matters for robots that need to know where they are.
ICRA7cULOC: Learning to Localize in Complex Large-Scale Environments with Ultra-Wideband RangesUltra-wideband radio ranging is a cheap way to locate a robot, but signals bounce off walls in large buildings in ways that make simple distance models give wrong answers.
ICRA6cMulti-Agent Path Finding Using Conflict-Based Search and Structural-Semantic Topometric MapsFinding collision-free paths for many robots at once on a detailed grid map takes too long to be practical in large spaces.
ICRA6cEphemerality Meets Lidar-Based Lifelong MappingA robot building a map over many sessions needs to remove objects that appear and disappear — like a parked car — but labeling things as simply moving or static is not enough to handle semi-permanent objects.
ICRA6cSLABIM: A SLAM-BIM Coupled Dataset in HKUST Main BuildingIndoor robot navigation datasets do not include the building's official floor-plan and structure data (called BIM), so researchers cannot test whether their maps match what the building actually looks like.
ICRA6cDiTer++: Diverse Terrain and Multi-Modal Dataset for Multi-Robot SLAM in Multi-Session EnvironmentsExisting datasets for mapping large areas with multiple robots cover only simple, controlled environments and single sessions, so algorithms developed on them may not work on real varied terrain.
ICRA6cHelmetPoser: A Helmet-Mounted IMU Dataset for Data-Driven Estimation of Human Head Motion in Diverse ConditionsCamera and laser sensors in helmets fail in dusty or smoky conditions, so there is a need to track head position using only the small motion sensors (IMUs) built into helmets, but no good dataset existed to train and test this.
ICRA6cDy3DGS-SLAM: Monocular 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Dynamic EnvironmentsExisting methods that build detailed 3D scene maps in real time (3DGS-SLAM) break when people or objects move through the scene, and they all require a depth sensor in addition to a regular camera.
IROS6cScalable Real2Sim: Physics-Aware Asset Generation Via Robotic Pick-and-Place SetupsMaking virtual copies of real objects for robot simulations takes a lot of manual work and special equipment.
ICRA5cLiLoc: Lifelong Localization Using Adaptive Submap Joining and Egocentric Factor GraphA robot that uses laser scans to know where it is over many months must handle environments that change over time and errors that build up across mapping sessions, without the map growing without bound.
ICRA5cMambaGlue: Fast and Robust Local Feature Matching with MambaDeep learning methods that match visual features across images are accurate but slow because they use attention mechanisms that scale poorly with the number of features.
ICRA5cGassidy: Gaussian Splatting SLAM in Dynamic EnvironmentsWhen a robot builds a 3D map of its surroundings from camera images, moving objects like people corrupt both the map and the robot's sense of where it is.
ICRA5cHGS-Planner: Hierarchical Planning Framework for Active Scene Reconstruction Using 3D Gaussian SplattingWhen a robot must map an unknown room on its own, it needs a real-time 3D model good enough to decide where to look next — which existing methods are either too slow or too low quality to support.
ICRA5cOpenGS-SLAM: Open-Set Dense Semantic SLAM with 3D Gaussian Splatting for Object-Level Scene UnderstandingRobots that map and label their surroundings can only recognize objects from a fixed list set at training time, so they miss anything outside that list.
IROS5cGSplatLoc: Grounding Keypoint Descriptors into 3D Gaussian Splatting for Improved Visual LocalizationA robot has to know exactly where it is using cameras, but existing methods are either slow or can't represent complex scenes well.
IROS5cTowards Robust Sensor-Fusion Ground SLAM: A Comprehensive Benchmark and A Resilient FrameworkExisting navigation systems don't have a standard way to test what breaks when conditions get tough, and they don't automatically switch between different sensors when some fail.
ICRA4cDifferentiable Composite Neural Signed Distance Fields for Robot Navigation in Dynamic Indoor EnvironmentsNavigation systems that use learned 3D shape representations must be fully retrained whenever furniture or objects move, which is too slow for practical use.
ICRA4cDARE: Diffusion Policy for Autonomous Robot ExplorationExploration planners that only react to what they can currently see can't plan paths that account for what's likely to be in the unexplored areas just out of sight.
ICRA4cRobot Navigation in Unknown and Cluttered Workspace with Dynamical System Modulation in Starshaped RoadmapNavigating a robot through a cluttered space is hampered when the free space is described with simple shapes like ellipses that don't fit the actual gaps, leaving usable paths undiscovered and causing dead ends.
ICRA4cHS-SLAM: Hybrid Representation with Structural Supervision for Improved Dense SLAMRobots that build a 3D map of a room while moving through it produce maps with holes and misaligned surfaces, especially when the camera moves fast or returns to a place it saw earlier.
ICRA4cMGSO: Monocular Real-Time Photometric SLAM with Efficient 3D Gaussian SplattingBuilding a detailed 3D map in real time from a single camera is slow, uses too much memory, and produces poor quality on ordinary laptops.
ICRA4cHier-SLAM: Scaling-Up Semantics in SLAM with a Hierarchically Categorical Gaussian SplattingAdding object-category labels to every point in a 3D Gaussian map works fine for a few categories but becomes too slow and memory-hungry when there are hundreds of categories.
ICRA4cIn-Pipe Navigation Development Environment and a Smooth Path Planning Method on Pipeline SurfaceResearchers building robots that inspect the inside of pipes had no shared simulation tool to test on, and planning smooth paths along curved pipe surfaces was an unsolved problem.
ICRA4cHGSLoc: 3DGS-Based Heuristic Camera Pose RefinementFiguring out exactly where a camera is in a known scene is slow or inaccurate when lighting or viewpoint changes a lot, especially without heavy neural network processing.
ICRA4cDeepVL: Dynamics and Inertial Measurements-based Deep Velocity Learning for Underwater OdometryUnderwater robots lose track of how fast they are moving when visibility drops or the camera sees very few features, causing position estimates to drift over long missions.
ICRA4cLLGS: Unsupervised Gaussian Splatting for Image Enhancement and Reconstruction in Pure Dark EnvironmentA 3D scene reconstruction method that uses many splats of color (3D Gaussian Splatting) breaks down in very dark images because dark photos from different angles look inconsistent with each other.
IROS4cKISS-SLAM: A Simple, Robust, and Accurate 3D LiDAR SLAM System With Enhanced Generalization CapabilitiesMost accurate 3D mapping systems for robots need extra sensors like GPS or motion chips and require a lot of tuning to work in new places.
ICRA3cSANDRO: A Robust Solver with a Splitting Strategy for Point Cloud RegistrationAligning two 3D point clouds from a sensor often fails when many of the matched points are wrong matches, as happens with real sensor data.
ICRA3cGaRLIO: Gravity Enhanced Radar-LiDAR-Inertial OdometryRobots that track their position using laser scans and an inertial sensor tend to drift vertically over time because gravity is estimated poorly without direct velocity information.
ICRA3cTopological Mapping for Traversability-Aware Long-Range Navigation in Off-Road TerrainAutonomous robots cannot reliably navigate long distances through unmarked forest because existing methods cannot assess which ground is safe to cross, explore unknown areas, and steer the robot all at once using only a camera and GPS.
ICRA3cLearning IMU Bias with Diffusion ModelThe error (bias) in motion sensors (IMUs) changes over time in an unpredictable way, and methods that predict a single fixed bias value cannot capture that uncertainty.
ICRA3cFast Online Learning of CLiFF-Maps in Changing EnvironmentsMaps that record how people typically move through a space become wrong over time when movement patterns change, and updating them from scratch is too slow.
ICRA3cFGO-SLAM: Enhancing Gaussian SLAM with Globally Consistent Opacity Radiance FieldMap-building systems based on 3D Gaussian blobs accumulate position errors and produce geometrically inaccurate surfaces, making them unreliable for tasks that need precise 3D maps.
IROS3cRayFronts: Open-Set Semantic Ray Frontiers for Online Scene Understanding and ExplorationA robot exploring a building needs a map that says what things are — not just where walls are — but doing this in real time for any category of object (not a fixed pre-set list) is too slow for current methods.
IROS3cVLM-Empowered Multi-Mode System for Efficient and Safe Planetary NavigationA planetary rover set to a single navigation strategy is either too slow on easy terrain or too risky on hard terrain, so no single mode works well across a whole mission.
IROS3cMARSCalib: Multi-robot, Automatic, Robust, Spherical Target-based Extrinsic Calibration in Field and Extraterrestrial EnvironmentsAligning the coordinate frames of cameras and LiDARs on outdoor or planetary robots is unreliable because sensors can be noisy or corrupted and flat calibration boards give poor LiDAR returns outdoors.
IROS3cTartanGround: A Large-Scale Dataset for Ground Robot Perception and NavigationThere's no big collection of robot sensor data covering different environment types and different robot body styles (wheeled vs. legged) that systems can learn from.
IROS3cFloPE: Flower Pose Estimation for Precision Pollination ↗A pollinating robot can't see flower positions and angles clearly because flowers look different, bunch together, and the robot's computer is weak.
IROS3cLeveraging Semantic Graphs for Efficient and Robust LiDAR SLAMRobot navigation systems that use LiDAR sensors get slow and unreliable in different real-world places because they only track individual points without understanding what things are.
IROS3cGaussianGraph: 3D Gaussian-Based Scene Graph Generation for Open-World Scene UnderstandingWhen robots try to understand 3D scenes using Gaussian splatting, they compress information into blobs but lose the ability to identify what objects are and where they sit relative to each other.
ICRA2cOne Map to Find Them All: Real-time Open-Vocabulary Mapping for Zero-shot Multi-Object NavigationWhen a robot looks for several objects one after another, it throws away everything it learned about the environment after each search and has to explore from scratch each time.
ICRA2cReinforcement Learning Driven Multi-Robot Exploration via Explicit Communication and Density-Based Frontier SearchWhen multiple robots explore an unknown space independently, they often scan the same areas repeatedly because they don't know what their teammates have already covered, wasting time and bandwidth.
ICRA2cLoGS: Visual Localization via Gaussian Splatting with Fewer Training ImagesFiguring out exactly where a camera is in 3D space is unreliable when you only have a small number of reference photos of the place.
ICRA2cErgodic Exploration over Meshable SurfacesPath planning methods that spread a robot's search time in proportion to how important each area is (ergodic search) only work on flat surfaces or simple curved shapes like spheres, not on complex real-world structures.
ICRA2cLeAP: Consistent multi-domain 3D labeling using Foundation ModelsLabeling 3D point cloud data by hand — tagging each point as road, wall, person, etc. — is very expensive, and automatic methods that borrow labels from 2D images produce inconsistent results in 3D.
ICRA2cMarginalizing and Conditioning Gaussians onto Linear Approximations of Smooth Manifolds with Applications in RoboticsWhen a robot tracks its own position and orientation, it needs to compute uncertainty estimates, but doing so correctly when the robot is constrained to move along a curved surface had no exact math solution.
ICRA2cIntrospective Loop Closure for SLAM with 4D Imaging RadarWhen a robot revisits a place it has seen before, radar-based mapping systems often fail to recognize it or, in plain-looking areas, think they have returned to a place they have not — both errors corrupt the map.
ICRA2cHelios: Heterogeneous Lidar Place Recognition via Overlap-Based Learning and Local Spherical TransformerA robot cannot reliably recognize a place it has visited before when it uses a different type of laser scanner (LiDAR) than the one used to build the map, because different scanners produce very different patterns of points.
ICRA2cGERA: Geometric Embedding for Efficient Point Registration AnalysisMatching two 3D point clouds to find how one relates to the other typically uses computationally expensive 3D convolutions and attention layers that are too slow for robots with limited computing power.
ICRA2cGnd: Global Navigation Dataset With Multi-Modal Perception and Multi-Category Traversability in Outdoor Campus EnvironmentsRobots navigating outdoors on university campuses need a large labeled dataset that tells them where they can safely walk or drive, but no such dataset covers multiple campuses with multiple sensor types and detailed terrain categories.
ICRA2cWildFusion: Multimodal Implicit 3D Reconstructions in the WildBuilding a 3D map of rough outdoor terrain that a legged robot can safely walk on requires combining many different sensor types, which existing 3D reconstruction methods do not support.
ICRA2cDynamem: Online Dynamic Spatio-Semantic Memory for Open World Mobile ManipulationMobile manipulation systems that remember where objects are break down when people move things around, because their memory never updates.
ICRA2cEnvoDat: A Large-Scale Multisensory Dataset for Robotic Spatial Awareness and Semantic Reasoning in Heterogeneous EnvironmentsMost robot datasets only cover normal city streets, leaving out difficult settings like dense vegetation, underground tunnels, fog, and total darkness where robots most often fail.
ICRA2cNYC-Event-VPR: A Large-Scale High-Resolution Event-Based Visual Place Recognition Dataset in Dense Urban EnvironmentsCameras that only record changes in light (event cameras) are promising for recognizing places, but there are almost no large public datasets to train or test them in real cities.
ICRA2cCollision-Aware Traversability Analysis for Autonomous Vehicles in the Context of Agricultural Robotics ↗A robot driving through a farm cannot tell which things blocking its path are soft plants it can push through and which are hard objects that will damage it.
ICRA2cMAC-VO: Metrics-Aware Covariance for Learning-Based Stereo Visual Odometry mac-vo.github.ioLearning-based stereo odometry systems — those that track position using two cameras — do not know how uncertain each matched point is in real-world units, so they pick points and weight errors poorly when computing the robot's path.
ICRA2cOnline Diffusion-Based 3D Occupancy Prediction at the Frontier with Probabilistic Map ReconciliationA robot exploring an unknown space cannot see around corners or into unvisited areas, so its map has blank regions that slow or block safe navigation.
ICRA2cNext-Best-Trajectory Planning of Robot Manipulators for Effective Observation and ExplorationA robot arm used to observe a dynamic scene needs to plan paths that collect the most useful visual information, but computing information gain fast enough to keep up with a moving scene is hard.
ICRA2cOnline Identification of Skidding Modes with Interactive Multiple Model EstimationRobots that steer by skidding their wheels behave very differently on different surfaces, and it is hard to figure out which type of skidding is happening while the robot is moving.
ICRA2cGraph2Nav: 3D Object-Relation Graph Generation to Robot NavigationA robot navigating a room needs to know not just where objects are but how they relate to each other, and building that kind of rich 3D map from 3D data directly is hard because labeled 3D training data is scarce.
ICRA2cContext Graph-Based Visual-Language Place RecognitionRecognizing a place from images is unreliable when lighting, seasons, or viewpoints change dramatically, and training a system to handle this requires large labeled datasets.
ICRA2cDOGE: An Extrinsic Orientation and Gyroscope Bias Estimation for Visual-Inertial Odometry InitializationCamera-IMU navigation systems become inaccurate over time if the physical alignment between the camera and IMU shifts, and current fixes only work once the robot is already moving enough to create depth in the images.
ICRA2cPoint2Graph: An End-to-End Point Cloud-Based 3D Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph for Robot NavigationRobots couldn't build a searchable map of a 3D space from point-cloud data alone — they also needed camera images with known positions, which are often unavailable.
ICRA2cMonocular Visual Place Recognition in LiDAR Maps via Cross-Modal State Space Model and Multi-View MatchingFiguring out where a regular camera is within a 3D laser-scan map is hard because photos and laser point clouds look nothing like each other.
IROS2cVSLAM-LAB: A Comprehensive Framework for Visual SLAM Methods and Datasets ↗Researchers who want to compare visual map-building systems (visual SLAM) spend most of their time fighting different code setups and data formats instead of doing science.
IROS2cGSO-SLAM: Robust Monocular SLAM with Global Structure OptimizationA single camera cannot reliably track its position in spaces with few visual features because there are not enough points to match between frames.
IROS2cHyla-SLAM: Toward Maximally Scalable 3D LiDAR-Based SLAM Using Dynamic Memory Management and Behavior TreesSLAM systems that map large areas waste memory storing everything at once, and changing how they work for different robots requires rewriting code.
IROS2cReal-time Spatial-temporal Traversability Assessment via Feature-based Sparse Gaussian ProcessGround robots driving on rough outdoor terrain need real-time maps showing where they can safely drive, and these maps need to combine old and new sensor data with uncertainty measures.
IROS2cAKF-LIO: LiDAR-Inertial Odometry with Gaussian Map by Adaptive Kalman FilterLiDAR odometry with gyro sensors uses a fixed noise guess that breaks down in bad spots: dirty air, moving people, or when data points are sparse.
IROS2cIntelligent LiDAR Navigation: Leveraging External Information and Semantic Maps with LLM as CopilotRobots using laser range finders can navigate around obstacles but cannot use text information that humans rely on, like "elevator is broken" or "this hallway is closed."
IROS2cFGS-SLAM: Fourier-based Gaussian Splatting for Real-time SLAM with Sparse and Dense Map Fusion3D mapping with a method called Gaussian Splatting is slow to start and creates too many or too few blurry shapes.
IROS2cOpenGS-Fusion: Open-Vocabulary Dense Mapping with Hybrid 3D Gaussian Splatting for Refined Object-Level UnderstandingMost ways to understand what's in a 3D scene are slow and rigid—they use fixed thresholds that don't adapt when lighting or angles change.
IROS2cArtGS: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Interactive Visual-Physical Modeling and Manipulation of Articulated ObjectsRobots can't grab and move objects with joints (like doors or robot arms) without knowing exactly where the joints are and how they move.
ICRA1c3DSSDF: Underwater 3D Sonar Reconstruction Using Signed Distance FunctionsUnderwater robots cannot use GPS and have limited sensors, making it very hard to know where they are or build a 3D map of the area around them.
ICRA1cTopology-Based Visual Active Room SegmentationSplitting an unknown indoor space into separate rooms is hard because standard methods need a complete map of the space before they can start, which is not possible during live exploration.
ICRA1cUR-MVO: Robust Monocular Visual Odometry for Underwater ScenariosStandard camera-based tracking systems break underwater because murky water, color shifts, and moving animals make it hard to find and match stable image features.
ICRA1cJoint Localization and Planning Using DiffusionA robot navigating indoors must figure out where it is on a map and plan a clear path at the same time, but most systems solve these two problems separately, which can cause errors to compound.
ICRA1cA Data-Driven Velocity Estimator for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles Experiencing Unmeasurable Flow and Wave DisturbanceSmall underwater vehicles in tight spaces like harbors get hit by bouncing waves and unpredictable currents that throw off standard speed and position estimates.
ICRA1cDeep Learning-Enhanced Visual Monitoring in Hazardous Underwater Environments with a Swarm of Micro-Robots ↗Small underwater robots drift and rotate unpredictably, so the images each one captures don't line up correctly when stitched together into a full view of the area.
ICRA1cIs Iteration Worth It? Revisit its Impact in Sliding-Window VIOIt is not clear when running extra refinement passes inside a robot's location-tracking system (visual-inertial odometry) is worth the extra computing cost on small, power-limited devices.
ICRA1cEVLoc: Event-Based Visual Localization in LiDAR Maps via Event-Depth RegistrationFiguring out where an event camera is inside a pre-built laser-scan map is hard because camera events and laser points are very different kinds of data and are difficult to line up geometrically.
ICRA1cVSS-SLAM: Voxelized Surfel Splatting for Geometally Accurate SLAMBuilding a 3D map of a new place using Gaussian-blob representations tends to produce overlapping and badly arranged blobs that make the geometry inaccurate.
ICRA1cSYNERGAI: Perception Alignment for Human-Robot CollaborationA robot and a person often have different views of the same space, and language-model-based systems ignore this mismatch, causing the robot to act on a world it does not actually see correctly.
ICRA1cTask-Aware Semantic Map: Autonomous Robot Task Assignment Beyond CommandsHome robots wait for people to tell them what to do instead of looking around and deciding on their own what needs doing.
ICRA1cActive Illumination for Visual Ego-Motion Estimation in the DarkA robot trying to track its own movement using a camera fails in the dark because there are not enough visible features to follow.
ICRA1cLiDAR Inertial Odometry and Mapping Using Learned Registration-Relevant FeaturesLaser-scanner mapping systems that process every scan point use a lot of memory and computing power, while hand-picked shortcuts lose accuracy.
ICRA1cInteractive4D: Interactive 4D LiDAR SegmentationWhen people manually label 3D lidar data, they have to click on each object in each scan one at a time, which takes a huge number of clicks for even a short sequence.
ICRA1cFLAF: Focal Line and Feature-Constrained Active View Planning for Visual Teach and RepeatA robot that navigates by matching camera images to a saved map fails in plain-looking places because there are no distinct visual features to match.
ICRA1cTunable Virtual IMU Frame by Weighted Averaging of Multiple Non-Collocated IMUsWhen several motion sensors (IMUs) are placed at different spots on a rigid body, their readings don't match each other and don't line up with where the camera or GPS sits, making it hard to combine them accurately.
ICRA1cOptimizing NeRF-Based SLAM with Trajectory Smoothness ConstraintsSimultaneous mapping and position-tracking systems that build photo-realistic 3D maps (NeRF-based SLAM) often estimate jerky, unrealistic camera paths, which hurts both position accuracy and map quality.
ICRA1cVisual Lidar Recursive Online Tracker (ViLiROT) for Autonomous Surface VesselsTracking other boats and objects from an autonomous boat using lidar keeps producing false tracks from things that are not actually moving.
ICRA1cInfield Self-Calibration of Intrinsic Parameters for Two Rigidly Connected IMUsTwo motion sensors (IMUs) mounted rigidly together have internal errors (biases and scale errors) that drift over time and must be corrected in the field without any external reference equipment.
ICRA1cJPG-SLAM: Joint Point-Gaussian Splatting Representation for Dense Dynamic SLAMBuilding a detailed, accurate map of a scene while a camera moves through it is especially hard when some objects in the scene are also moving, because the same representation has to track the camera's position and capture both still and moving parts.
ICRA1cM3DSS: A Multi-Platform, Multi-Sensor, and Multi-Scenario Dataset for SLAM SystemExisting test collections for robot mapping software use only a few sensor types and movement styles, so they hide weaknesses that show up in fast motion, dark environments, or plain-looking spaces.
ICRA1cRISED: Accurate and Efficient RGB-Colorized Mapping Using Image Selection and Point Cloud DensificationWhen you color a 3D laser scan with camera photos, using every photo blurs the colors because images taken from the wrong angle do not line up perfectly with the scan points.
ICRA1cLiteVLoc: Map-Lite Visual Localization for Image Goal NavigationNavigating to a photographed destination in a large building requires knowing exactly where the robot is, but storing the dense 3D maps normally used for that takes too much space.
ICRA1cCascade IPG Observer for Underwater Robot State EstimationUnderwater robots lose track of where they are and how fast they are moving when GPS or other outside positioning is cut off.
ICRA1cUncertainty-Aware Visual-Inertial SLAM with Volumetric Occupancy MappingSystems that track a robot's position using cameras and inertial sensors do not produce accurate solid 3D maps that also account for how uncertain each depth reading is.
ICRA1cIntegrating Multi-Robot Adaptive Sampling and Informative Path Planning for Spatiotemporal Natural Environment PredictionA group of robots trying to map a changing environment (like water temperature or gas concentration) must decide both where to take measurements and what path to travel, but solving both problems together is very hard.
ICRA1cFast Global Localization on Neural Radiance FieldFinding a robot's position inside a scene stored as a neural 3D model (NeRF) is accurate but very slow because the method has to render a fake image for every candidate position it considers.
ICRA1cImproving Indoor Localization Accuracy by Using an Efficient Implicit Neural Map RepresentationStandard grid-based maps used for indoor robot localization are too coarse to capture fine geometric detail from laser scans, limiting position accuracy.
ICRA1cKey-Scan-Based Mobile Robot Navigation: Integrated Mapping, Planning, and Control Using Graphs of Scan Regions ↗A robot exploring an unknown cluttered space needs a single system that can build a map, plan a route, and move safely all at once, with a mathematical proof that it will reach its goal without hitting anything.
ICRA1cCAO-RONet: A Robust 4D Radar Odometry with Exploring More Information from Low-Quality Points4D radar gives a robot speed and range data that work in rain and fog, but the point clouds it produces are too sparse and noisy to estimate the robot's motion accurately.
ICRA1cSliceOcc: Indoor 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction with Vertical Slice RepresentationPredicting which parts of an indoor room are occupied and by what type of object is hard from cameras alone because flat top-down or side views miss detail in cluttered, heavily blocked spaces.
ICRA1cRobust Scene Change Detection Using Visual Foundation Models and Cross-Attention MechanismsDetecting what has changed between two photos of the same place is difficult when lighting, season, or camera angle differ between the photos.
ICRA1cKeypoint Detection and Description for Raw Bayer ImagesRobot cameras normally send raw image data through a processing chip before any vision software can use it, which adds cost, delay, and extra hardware.
ICRA1cDVLO4D: Deep Visual-Lidar Odometry with Sparse Spatial-Temporal Fusion ↗Tracking a robot's position using both cameras and laser scanners is hard because the two sensors don't line up perfectly and the system forgets information from earlier moments, causing position errors that build up over time.
ICRA1cConfiguration-Adaptive Visual Relative Localization for Spherical Modular Self-Reconfigurable RobotsRobots made of modules that can rearrange themselves change their own shape over time, so existing visual localization methods — which assume a fixed body — can't track how separate assemblies are positioned relative to each other.
ICRA1cNeural Surface Reconstruction and Rendering for LiDAR-Visual SystemsCombining laser scanner depth data with camera images to get both accurate 3D geometry and realistic-looking images is hard because the two representations don't connect naturally.
ICRA1cMulti-Modality Test-Time Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation in Robotic PerceptionA robot's scene-understanding model trained in one environment degrades in a different one, and existing fixes only handle one sensor type like a camera, not camera plus laser scanner together.
ICRA1cNon-Destructive 3D Root Structure ModelingMapping the 3D shape of plant roots underground without digging them up is hard because radar scans of the soil are noisy and make it difficult to find and locate buried objects.
ICRA1cIMOST: Incremental Memory Mechanism with Online Self-Supervision for Continual Traversability LearningA legged robot learning which ground is safe to walk on in real time tends to forget what it learned earlier and makes biased predictions in changing scenes.
ICRA1cOnline Multi-Robot Federated Learning for Distributed Coverage Control of Unknown Spatial Processes ↗A team of robots trying to cover an area needs to learn what the environment looks like, but sharing raw sensor data between robots uses too much bandwidth and raises privacy concerns.
ICRA1cOnline Informative Motion Planning for Active Information Gathering of a Non-Stationary Gaussian ProcessMapping physical fields like ocean depth is hard when the field varies in unpredictable ways across space and the robot has no prior model of it.
ICRA1cOpenSU3D: Open World 3D Scene Understanding Using Foundation ModelsSystems that label 3D environments struggle to scale because they store data for every single point, and they fail when asked questions that need context rather than just appearance.
ICRA1cNew Graph Distance Measures and Matching of Topological Maps for Robotic ExplorationWhen a robot builds a map of an area as a network of connected places, comparing two such maps to check if they match is not well-defined mathematically.
ICRA1cRE-TRIP: Reflectivity Instance Augmented Triangle Descriptor for 3D Place RecognitionA robot using a laser scanner (LiDAR) to recognize places it has visited before fails in long corridors or on bridges because those spaces all look the same geometrically.
ICRA1cTCAFF: Temporal Consistency for Robot Frame AlignmentWhen two robots work together without GPS, their maps slowly drift out of sync because they have no shared reference point to start from.
ICRA1cRadar4VoxMap: Accurate Odometry from Blurred Radar ObservationsRadar-only tracking of a robot's position drifts over time because radar scans are blurry and noisy, making it hard to match new scans against the stored map.
ICRA1cLuVo: Lunar Visual Odometry Using Homography-Based Image Feature MatchingNavigating on the Moon by comparing left and right camera images fails when the ground all looks the same and the cameras are far apart.
ICRA1cS2BEV: Lightweight, Robust, and Precise SLAM-Oriented Segmentation Bird Eye's View Mapping ApproachRobots working in orchards need accurate maps that can be built and updated quickly, but orchards change constantly and are too unstructured for standard mapping tools to handle efficiently.
ICRA1cSuite-IN: Aggregating Motion Features from Apple Suite for Robust Inertial NavigationTracking a pedestrian's position using only the motion sensor in one wearable device is inaccurate because each device placement picks up different motion artifacts.
ICRA1cSubmodular Optimization for Keyframe Selection & Usage in SLAMLiDAR mapping systems use crude rules to decide which scans to save and how to use them, wasting storage and compute.
ICRA1cAdaptive Thresholding for Sequence-Based Place RecognitionA robot using cameras to recognize where it has been before needs a hand-tuned cutoff value to decide if two images show the same place, and no one had a way to set that value automatically.
ICRA1cDynORecon: Dynamic Object Reconstruction for NavigationStandard 3D mapping systems assume the world is still, so moving objects leave ghost artifacts in the map and the free-space estimate becomes wrong.
ICRA1cMT-PCR: Leveraging Modality Transformation for Large-Scale Point Cloud Registration with Limited OverlapAligning two large 3D laser scans taken kilometers apart is slow and fails when the two scans share very little overlapping area.
ICRA1cDVN-SLAM: Dynamic Visual Neural Slam Based on Local-Global EncodingNeural map-building systems that store scenes as continuous math functions (neural implicit maps) fail when moving objects are in the scene and produce blurry or uncertain renderings.
ICRA1cRE0: Recognize Everything with 3D Zero-Shot Instance SegmentationSegmenting individual objects in a 3D scene and naming them is hard to do without training a model specifically on 3D data, and existing methods produce labels that are inconsistent between camera views.
ICRA1cEnd-to-End Underwater Multi-View Stereo for Dense Scene Reconstruction3D reconstruction models trained on normal above-water images fail underwater because light bends and scatters differently there, and no large training dataset of underwater scenes with known depths existed.
ICRA1cOpen-RGBT: Open-Vocabulary RGB-T Zero-Shot Semantic Segmentation in Open-World EnvironmentsImage segmentation systems that combine normal cameras with heat cameras only work on a fixed list of pre-defined object categories and cannot recognize new ones.
ICRA1cOverlapping Free: Anchorless UWB-Assisted Relative Pose Estimation for Multi-Robot SystemsRobots trying to find each other's position using cameras or lasers need to be facing each other or close enough to share a field of view, which is often not possible.
ICRA1cNeuraloc: Visual Localization in Neural Implicit Map With Dual Complementary FeaturesMethods that store a 3D scene as a neural network (NeRF) for camera localization either use too much storage or lack enough geometric information to be accurate.
ICRA1cElite-EvGS: Learning Event-based 3D Gaussian Splatting by Distilling Event-to-Video PriorsBuilding a detailed 3D scene model from an event camera is hard because the data is very sparse, which makes starting the reconstruction poorly and leaves large areas with too few views to constrain the model.
ICRA1cEfficient Trajectory Generation Based on Traversable Planes in 3D Complex Architectural SpacesPlanning a smooth path for a ground robot through a large building with multiple floors, ramps, and stairs is slow because the full 3D environment is very complex to work with.
ICRA1cA Refined 3D Gaussian Representation for High-Quality Dynamic Scene ReconstructionRepresenting moving scenes as collections of 3D Gaussian blobs (3D Gaussian Splatting) uses a lot of memory and produces noisy results where objects move.
ICRA1cMagnetometer-Calibrated Hybrid Transformer for Robust Inertial Tracking in RoboticsTracking position using only motion sensors (IMU) drifts badly over long distances because the sensors accumulate small errors and the compass signal (magnetometer) is rarely used well.
ICRA1cEPRecon: An Efficient Framework for Real-Time Panoptic 3D Reconstruction from Monocular VideoBuilding a detailed 3D map with object labels from a single moving camera is too slow for real-time use because estimating depth by comparing multiple camera views is very expensive.
IROS1cPIPE Planner: Pathwise Information Gain with Map Predictions for Indoor Robot ExplorationWhen a robot explores a building, methods that only check how much new area a single waypoint would reveal miss out on coverage gained along the whole path, but computing coverage for entire paths is slow and tends to overcount unknown space.
IROS1cVisual Loop Closure Detection Through Deep Graph ConsensusA mapping robot needs to recognize when it has returned to a place it visited before, but checking each candidate location one at a time with deep image matching misses agreement across nearby locations and can be too slow.
IROS1cTiny LiDARs for Manipulator Self-Awareness: Sensor Characterization and Initial Localization ExperimentsSmall, low-resolution distance sensors give noisy readings that change depending on how far away and at what angle the target is, making it hard to know where an object is in 3D space.
IROS1cOpenVox: Real-time Instance-level Open-vocabulary Probabilistic Voxel RepresentationMobile robots need 3D maps that identify individual objects by name in real time, but existing systems are too slow or too fragile when sensors or segmentation make errors.
IROS1cTask-driven SLAM Benchmarking for Robot NavigationTests for robot mapping and localization systems (SLAM) mostly measure map accuracy but ignore whether the robot can reliably return to the same spot repeatedly — which is what actually matters for navigation tasks.
IROS1cBag-of-Word-Groups (BoWG): A Robust and Efficient Loop Closure Detection Method Under Perceptual AliasingInside repetitive environments like narrow pipes, standard visual place-recognition methods get confused because many locations look nearly identical, causing wrong loop-closure matches.
IROS1cDynamicGSG: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Scene Graphs for Environment AdaptationWhen a robot works on a task for days, the scene changes (things move, get added, get removed) but the robot's 3D map can't update quickly enough to keep track.
IROS1cTarget Localization and Following Based on LiDAR and Ultra-Wideband Ranging with Consideration of Target VisibilityA robot following a specific person using laser scans often confuses that person with others who look similar and loses track when something blocks the view.
IROS1cMPDG-SLAM: Motion Probability-Based 3DGS-SLAM in Dynamic EnvironmentBuilding a 3D map with a moving camera in a scene that also has moving people or objects is difficult, and the usual way to remove moving things uses a slow optical-flow model that does not run fast enough for mobile devices.
IROS1cRobust and Real-Time Perception and Planning for UGVs in Complex Outdoor EnvironmentsGround robots driving outdoors miss low-lying and fast-moving obstacles that laser scanners overlook, and they get stuck when the planned destination is physically blocked.
IROS1cDISCOVERSE: Efficient Robot Simulation in Complex High-Fidelity EnvironmentsExisting robot simulators do not combine photorealistic scene reconstruction from real video with accurate physics in one pipeline, making it hard to train robots in simulation and then transfer that training to the real world.
IROS1cSCORE: Saturated Consensus Relocalization in Semantic Line MapsFinding a camera's position using maps made of labeled lines fails when almost all the candidate line matches are wrong — sometimes up to 99.5% are incorrect.
IROS1cGO-VMP: Global Optimization for View Motion Planning in Fruit MappingA robot monitoring fruit in an orchard needs to see as many fruits as possible while traveling as little as possible, but existing view-planning methods optimize one goal and sacrifice the other.
IROS1cPC-SRIF: Preconditioned Cholesky-based Square Root Information Filter for Vision-aided Inertial NavigationA type of filter used for robot navigation (square root information filter) becomes numerically unstable in low-precision arithmetic because the math matrix it operates on is poorly conditioned, forcing the use of a slower decomposition method.
IROS1cLegged Robot State Estimation Using Invariant Neural-Augmented Kalman Filter with a Neural CompensatorA standard math-based filter for tracking a walking robot's position and orientation loses accuracy over time because the real world is more complex than the filter's simplified math can handle.
IROS1cLiMo-Calib: On-Site Fast LiDAR-Motor Calibration for Quadruped Robot-Based Panoramic 3D Sensing SystemThe vibrations from a walking four-legged robot keep shifting the alignment between its spinning laser scanner and the motor turning it, so the 3D map it builds slowly becomes inaccurate.
IROS1cSpatial Graph Attentional Network Based Place Recognition with Visual Mamba EmbeddingRecognizing a place from a photo gets unreliable when lighting or seasons change, and the usual step of checking geometry to confirm a match (RANSAC) is slow.
IROS1cAcoustic Neural 3D Reconstruction Under Pose DriftBuilding a 3D map from sonar images breaks down quickly if the sensor's position estimates drift even a little, because current methods assume you know exactly where the sensor was.
IROS1cSAGENet: Binaural Echo-Based 3D Depth Estimation with Sparse Angular Queries and Refined Geometric CuesEstimating distances using only the two-microphone echoes of a room produces depth maps that drift in scale and shape because the system does not use the clear geometric information already present in the echo signal.
IROS1cUnderwater target 6D State Estimation via UUV Attitude Enhance ObservabilityA single underwater robot needs to track the position and orientation of a target object using only noisy sound-range readings, with no GPS or outside help.
IROS1cAGCNet: Improving Inertial Odometry via IMU Accelerometer and Gyroscope Online CompensationSmall errors in an inertial sensor's accelerometer and gyroscope readings build up over time and cause position estimates to drift.
IROS1cGenerating Actionable Robot Knowledge Bases by Combining 3D Scene Graphs with Robot OntologiesRobots and simulators each describe the world in different file formats that do not talk to each other, so a robot cannot automatically turn a scene description into knowledge it can reason about.
IROS1cREACT: Real-time Efficient Attribute Clustering and Transfer for Updatable 3D Scene GraphRobots that build maps of their surroundings cannot quickly update those maps when objects get moved.
IROS1cConsistent Pose Estimation of Unmanned Ground Vehicles through Terrain-Aided Multi-Sensor Fusion on Geometric ManifoldsStandard GPS and sensor fusion systems for ground vehicles assume flat terrain, so on hills or rocky ground they become inaccurate and unpredictable, and tuning them is different for every terrain type.
IROS1cPerpetua: Multi-Hypothesis Persistence Modeling for Semi-Static EnvironmentsRobots can't predict if a door will be open or closed the next time they see the room—features appear and disappear unpredictably, so maps become outdated.
IROS1cP2 Explore: Efficient Exploration in Unknown Cluttered Environment with Floor Plan PredictionRobots exploring cluttered indoor spaces get stuck because they can't predict room layouts well enough to pick good exploration routes.
IROS1cObservability Investigation for Rotational Calibration of (Global-pose aided) VIO under Straight Line MotionGoing straight means some camera-and-gyro angle settings can't be figured out, but this was wrong in old papers.
IROS1cCAMSCKF: A Multi-State Constraint Kalman Filter with Adaptive Multivariate Noise Parameters Clustering and Estimation for Visual-Inertial OdometryWhen robots try to figure out where they are using cameras and motion sensors outdoors, the sensor noise changes over time and isn't the same everywhere.
IROS1cSpectral-Temporal Attention for Robust Change DetectionSystems for spotting changes in pictures work on satellite images or street photos but fail when you switch between them or look at indoor spaces.
IROS1cBenchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Localization in Indoor Environments under Substantial Static and Dynamic Scene ChangesExisting datasets for testing indoor robot navigation don't have long sequences showing real rooms, precise location truth, and real changes to the space over time.
IROS1cSPADE: Towards Scalable Path Planning Architecture on Actionable Multi-Domain 3D ScenE GraphsPlanning a path for a robot in a map that is structured as layers is slow because every small obstacle in the way forces the planner to restart from scratch.
IROS1cMesh-Learner: Texturing Mesh with Spherical HarmonicsScene reconstruction with neural networks makes pictures that look great but can't work with normal 3D tools like Blender or simulators.
IROS1cDnD Filter: Differentiable State Estimation for Dynamic Systems using Diffusion ModelsTracking the state of a system with shaking sensors assumes noise follows a bell curve, which doesn't fit real data and loses accuracy.
IROS1cHybrid Transformer-Mamba Model for 3D Semantic SegmentationMethods for labeling 3D point cloud data slow down a lot when trying to understand far-away relationships, while simpler methods miss fine details.
IROS1cFloorplan-SLAM: A Real-Time, High-Accuracy, and Long-Term Multi-Session Point-Plane SLAM for Efficient Floorplan ReconstructionMaking accurate floor plans of big buildings in real time without expensive sensors or slow offline processing has not been possible.
IROS1cDogLegs: Robust Proprioceptive State Estimation for Legged Robots Using Multiple Leg-Mounted IMUsLegged robot state estimation degrades in extreme environments where exteroceptive sensors are unreliable, and body-only IMU fusion accumulates drift without robust contact detection.
IROS1cUltra-Wideband assisted Visual-Inertial Localization Correction System with Position-Unknown UWB AnchorsA robot using cameras and motion sensors drifts over time, and existing radio-based fixes need the radio anchors to be measured in advance, which is hard to do at scale.
IROS1cRA-NeRF: Robust Neural Radiance Field Reconstruction with Accurate Camera Pose Estimation under Complex TrajectoriesWhen building a 3D scene from pictures, wrong camera position guesses make bad 3D models, especially when the camera moves in twisty paths.
IROS1cSplatPose: Geometry-Aware 6-DoF Pose Estimation from Single RGB Image via 3D Gaussian SplattingFinding an object's exact position and rotation from a single photo is ambiguous because you cannot tell which way the object is rotated without depth information.
IROS1cGLIC-Calib: Targetless and One-Shot Spatial-Temporal Calibration of LiDAR-IMU-Camera for Ground VehiclesYou can't tell where the laser, motion sensors, and camera sit on a ground robot without placing markers or taking lots of measurements.
ICRAUnified Adaptive and Cooperative Planning Using Multi-Task Coregionalized Gaussian ProcessesA team of robots mapping a changing environment must decide whether to go to new places or go back and recheck places that may have changed — both matter and it is hard to do both well.
ICRAHeterogeneous Exploration and Monitoring with Online Free-Space Ellipsoid GraphsIn an unknown environment, fast scout robots and slower worker robots need to split up their jobs cleanly — scouts map the space while workers check specific targets — but coordinating them efficiently is hard.
ICRAAn Algorithm for Geometric Navigation Planning Under Uncertainty Using Terrain Boundary DetectionA simple robot that can only detect terrain boundaries must navigate to a goal area despite significant uncertainty in how far it actually turns when commanded, and no standard GPS or map-matching is available.
ICRADGS-SLAM: A Visual Dense SLAM Based on Gaussian Splatting in Dynamic EnvironmentsA robot trying to map a scene and track its own position gets confused when people or other moving objects are present, because those movements corrupt the map.
ICRAPlanarNeRF: Online Learning of Planar Primitives with Neural Radiance FieldsFinding all the flat surfaces in a 3D scene from a moving camera in real time is hard because you need to match the same surface across many frames and most methods work only after all the data is collected.
ICRAWinding Number-Guided Edge-Preserving Implicit Neural Representation of CAD SurfacesRebuilding a 3D surface from a raw cloud of scanned points is hard when the scan has no surface-direction data, because the result tends to blur sharp edges.
ICRADetailRefine: Towards Fine-Grained and Efficient Online Monocular 3D ReconstructionBuilding a 3D model of a room in real time from a single moving camera wastes effort refining flat surfaces, ignores which camera angles give the most useful information, and loses fine details when thinning the voxel grid.
ICRADiver to Robot Communication UnderwaterGetting an underwater robot to understand a diver's hand-signal sequences is unreliable because underwater video makes individual gestures hard to recognize correctly.
ICRAActive Semantic Mapping with Mobile Manipulator in Horticultural EnvironmentsA farm robot with a limited camera view needs to build a complete, labeled map of plants for counting and picking, but choosing where to look next is slow and uncertain.
ICRACELLmap: Enhancing LiDAR SLAM Through Elastic and Lightweight Spherical Map Representation3D maps built by robots with laser scanners take up too much storage and are hard to use for other tasks after they are built.
ICRAUnder Pressure: Altimeter-Aided ICP for 3D Maps ConsistencyWhen a robot scans an environment like a vertical shaft that has few distinct geometric features, its scan-matching (ICP) position estimate drifts badly up and down over time.
