IROS1cVertiSelector: Automatic Curriculum Learning for Wheeled Mobility on Vertically Challenging TerrainTraining robots to climb steep hills with learning fails quickly and doesn't work on new terrain because training is random and covers too much ground.
IROS1cHigh-Precision Transformer-Based Visual Servoing for Humanoid Robots in Aligning Tiny Objects ↗Humanoid robots cannot see well enough to put a screwdriver tip or other tiny tool exactly where a screw sits.
IROS1cPreference Aligned Diffusion Planner for Quadrupedal Locomotion ControlWalk-planning networks trained in simulation fail on real robots doing gaits the training data didn't have much of.
IROS1cNuExo: A Wearable Exoskeleton Covering all Upper Limb ROM for Outdoor Data Collection and Teleoperation of Humanoid RobotsExisting gloves and arm devices can't track all the ways a human arm moves naturally, and they're too heavy and complex to wear outside in the real world.
IROS1cAwakening Facial Emotional Expressions in Human-RobotRobot faces need new expressions programmed by hand each time, which is slow and limits how expressive they can become.
ICRAOptimal Torque Distribution via Dynamic Adaptation for Quadrupedal Locomotion on Slippery TerrainsA four-legged robot slips and loses balance on low-friction surfaces because standard controllers distribute forces across legs without accounting for how likely each foot is to slip.
ICRAAdded Mass and Accuracy of the FF-SLIP Model for Legged SwimmingA simplified math model used to study legged swimming robots was missing a force that water exerts on a moving leg—the force needed to push water out of the way.
ICRAHigh Accuracy Aerial Maneuvers on Legged Robots using Variational Integrator Discretized Trajectory OptimizationWhen planning a flip or jump for a legged robot, the math that predicts where the body lands builds up error over the long airborne phase, causing the robot to land at the wrong angle.
ICRABeyond Robustness: Learning Unknown Dynamic Load Adaptation for Quadruped Locomotion on Rough TerrainA four-legged robot carrying an unknown shifting load on rough ground tends to stumble because it cannot easily tell how the load is moving.
ICRAInformed Repurposing of Quadruped Legs for New TasksIn remote places like space or the deep sea, you cannot build new robot parts, so you need to know in advance which existing leg pieces can handle a new job.
ICRATunable Leg Stiffness in a Monopedal Hopper for Energy-Efficient Vertical Hopping Across Varying Ground ProfilesA hopping robot with a fixed spring in its leg wastes energy on some ground types because the leg stiffness doesn't match what the ground requires for an efficient bounce.
ICRAIndoor and Outdoor Multi-Terrain Stair-Climbing Robot DesignWheeled robots climbing stairs tend to pitch forward or backward badly, which wastes energy and can cause falls.
ICRASimplifying Reward Design in Complex Robotics: Average-Reward Maximum Entropy Reinforcement LearningTraining a robot to balance a double pendulum requires carefully hand-crafting a reward signal, and small mistakes in that reward make the trained behavior fragile.
ICRAGenerating Diverse Challenging Terrains for Legged Robots Using Quality-Diversity Algorithm ↗Finding a wide range of terrain shapes that expose different weaknesses in a walking robot's controller is not done in any systematic way.
ICRAEnhancing Robotic System Robustness via Lyapunov Exponent-Based OptimizationThere is no practical, math-friendly way to measure how stable a complex robot with many joints and contacts is, making it hard to automatically tune a controller for stability.
ICRAA Data-Driven Contact Estimation Method for Wheeled-Biped Robots ↗Knowing whether a wheeled-biped robot's wheels are touching the ground is important for control, but existing methods assume a walking gait or require dedicated contact sensors that these robots do not have.
ICRAUser-Aware Collaborative Learning in Human-Robot InteractionsSocial robots frustrate people during collaborative tasks because they do not adapt their decisions to how annoyed or impatient the user is becoming.
ICRALearn to Swim: Data-Driven LSTM Hydrodynamic Model for Quadruped Robot Gait Optimization ↗To make a four-legged underwater robot walk efficiently, you need to know the water forces on its legs accurately, but standard physics formulas are too simple to capture how water actually pushes on moving legs.
ICRAMotionGlot: A Multi-Embodied Motion Generation ModelGenerating natural movement for robots with very different bodies — a four-legged dog versus a human — from a text description usually requires a separate trained model for each body type.
ICRASingle-Stage Optimization of Open-Loop Stable Limit Cycles with Smooth, Symbolic DerivativesFinding a repeating, stable walking gait for a legged robot by optimizing the motion path and checking stability usually requires multiple separate steps, which is slow and does not generalize across robot designs.
ICRAA Novel Telelocomotion Framework with CoM Estimation for Scalable Locomotion on Humanoid RobotsRemote-control interfaces for humanoid robots walking over uneven ground cannot translate the human operator's walking intent into stable robot steps.
ICRAAngular Divergent Component of Motion: A Step Towards Planning Spatial DCM Objectives for Legged Robots ↗Existing balance planning tools for legged robots only handle forward and sideways motion; they do not account for the robot's body rotating, so full balance planning is incomplete.
ICRAMusic-Driven Legged Robots: Synchronized Walking to Rhythmic BeatsLegged robot walking controllers are not designed to match a specific beat or stay in phase with changing music.
ICRASKOOTR: A Skating, Omni-Oriented, Tripedal RobotThree-legged robots can spin in place easily but walk inefficiently because they have to turn themselves around between every step to face the direction they want to go.
ICRAWaLTER: A Wheel and Leg Tumbling Expedition RobotWheeled robots move fast on flat ground but cannot climb stairs, while legged robots handle rough terrain but are slow and energy-hungry on flat surfaces.
ICRAResettable Land Anchor Launcher for Unmanned Rover Rescue and Slope ClimbingA planetary rover stuck on a steep slope or in loose soil has no way to free itself because there is no crew or rescue vehicle nearby.
ICRAEnhancing Robotic Perception with Low-Cost Fast Active Vision Achieving Sub-Millimeter Accurate Marker-Based Pose EstimationRobots that move around need to know where objects are very precisely and very fast, even when lighting changes or objects are partly hidden, but existing solutions are expensive or slow.
ICRATHAMP-3D: Tangent-Based Hybrid A* Motion Planning for Tethered Robots in Sloped 3D TerrainsPlanning paths for a wheeled robot attached to a cable on a steep slope is hard because the cable can go slack, tip the robot over, or wrap around rocks.
ICRAMPC-QP-Based Control Framework for Compliant Behavior of Humanoid Robots in Physical Collaboration with HumansA humanoid robot helping a person carry a heavy object must push and pull compliantly without losing its balance, which standard rigid controllers cannot do.
ICRAFinite-Step Capturability and Recursive Feasibility for Bipedal Walking in Constrained RegionsPredictive footstep planners for two-legged robots can run out of valid next steps in tight spaces because they cannot see far enough ahead to avoid trapping themselves.
ICRAUGotMe: An Embodied System for Affective Human-Robot InteractionA humanoid robot trying to read emotions during a group conversation gets confused by faces of bystanders and by people who are not currently speaking.
ICRAWallbounce: Push Wall to Navigate with Contact-Implicit MPCA ball-balancing robot with limited motors cannot speed up, slow down, or dodge obstacles quickly using only its drive mechanism.
ICRAA Virtual Gravity Controller for Efficient Underactuated Biped RobotsA two-legged robot with few motors cannot copy the smooth, low-energy walking that a passive mechanical system would produce on a slope if placed on flat ground.
ICRAUnsupervised Domain Adaptation for Gait State EstimationA model trained to read walking patterns from normal walking data stops working well when the person is wearing an exoskeleton, and labeling new data for each device is too expensive to scale.
ICRADeep Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Payload Transport in Biped-Wheeled RobotsGetting two wheeled-legged robots to carry a shared load together along a path requires them to stay in sync, stay stable, and not fight each other's motion — all at once.
ICRAA Tugging Controller that Maximizes Lateral Resistive Force by Mounding Sandy TerrainA rover trying to anchor itself by pushing sand sideways gets only a brief peak of grip before the sand pile collapses, and the timing of that peak varies with the ground.
ICRAFine-Tuning Hard-to-Simulate Objectives for Quadruped Locomotion: A Case Study on Total Power SavingTraining a walking robot in simulation cannot reliably reduce real battery drain because simulators do not model electrical power use accurately.
ICRAPitching Motion in a Humanoid Robot Using Human-Inspired Shoulder Elastic Energy and Motor Torque OptimizationHumanoid robots cannot throw as fast or as efficiently as humans because they lack a way to store and release energy at the shoulder the way human tendons and muscles do.
ICRAMastering Agile Jumping Skills from Simple Practices with Iterative Learning ControlTeaching a legged robot to jump accurately to a specific target is hard because once it leaves the ground there is nothing to control, and small errors add up to big misses.
ICRASuPLE: Robot Learning with Lyapunov RewardsDesigning a reward signal for a robot to learn from usually needs an expert and often requires starting the robot from many random positions — which is unsafe or impractical on real hardware.
ICRALyapunov-Certified Trajectory Tracking for Mobile Robot With a Tail Wheel: Differential-Flatness and Adaptive Backstepping DesignA three-wheeled robot with a tail wheel is hard to steer precisely because the tail wheel adds a mechanical lag that ties the turning rate to the steering angle in a tricky way.
ICRAA Control Scheme for Collaborative Object Transportation between a Human and a Quadruped Robot Using the MIGHTY Suction CupA four-legged robot trying to carry an object together with a human tends to either let the object slip or resist the human's guiding force too much.
ICRARobust Reinforcement Learning-Based Locomotion for Resource-Constrained Quadrupeds with Exteroceptive Sensing ↗Small, low-power four-legged robots cannot easily climb stairs because processing depth-camera images in real time drains their limited compute budget.
ICRAPROBE: Proprioceptive Obstacle Detection and Estimation while Navigating in ClutterLegged robots moving through cluttered or dark spaces cannot use cameras to spot obstacles they cannot see.
ICRAContact Force Estimation for a Leg-Wheel Transformable Robot With Varying Contact PointsMeasuring how hard a robot's leg-wheel touches the ground is hard when the robot can roll and walk, because the contact point moves continuously around the wheel surface.
ICRAInterpretable Active Inference Gait Control Learning ↗Getting a legged robot to walk steadily in rough outdoor conditions requires a controller that can adapt on the fly to unexpected disturbances without being reprogrammed.
ICRAEffective Self-Righting Strategies for Elongate Multi-Legged RobotsLong multi-legged robots that tip over on rough ground cannot reliably get back upright on their own.
ICRADynamic Bipedal MPC with Foot-Level Obstacle Avoidance and Adjustable Step TimingTwo-legged robots have no real-time planner that can at the same time dodge obstacles at the body level, pick safe footholds around ground obstacles, and adjust when to take each step.
ICRAExploration and Analysis of Torso-Limb Coordination of Quadruped Walkers with Compliant TorsoIt is not well understood how a flexible (compliant) spine in a four-legged robot changes the way the robot walks, or whether the front or back legs should do most of the pushing.
ICRAPinto: A Latched Spring Actuated Robot for Jumping and PerchingNo existing small legged robot could jump from the ground, land on a vertical tree trunk, and hold on — the way squirrels do.
ICRAKoopman Operator Based Linear Model Predictive Control for Quadruped TrottingControlling a four-legged robot in real time is hard: simple linear models are inaccurate, and accurate nonlinear solvers are too slow to run in real time.
ICRAInternal-Stably Energy-Saving Cooperative Control of Articulated Wheeled Robot with Distributed Drive UnitsA wheeled robot made of linked segments, each with its own motor, can become unstable or waste energy if the motors don't coordinate their forces well.
ICRAEnhancing Navigation Efficiency of Quadruped Robots via Leveraging Personal Transportation Platforms ↗Four-legged robots use a lot of energy and cannot travel far distances on their own legs alone.
ICRARINA: Rapid Introspective Neural Adaptation for Out-of-Distribution Payload Configurations on Quadruped RobotsA four-legged robot's walking controller breaks down when a new, unusually heavy or oddly placed load is attached, and retraining it takes too long to be practical.
ICRABio-Inspired Distributed Neural Locomotion Controller (D-NLC) for Robust Locomotion and Emergent BehaviorsMost legged robot controllers run on one central computer and break down badly when a leg is damaged or the terrain is very uneven.
ICRA3D Whole-Body Pose Estimation Using Graph High-Resolution Network for Humanoid Robot TeleoperationEstimating the full 3D pose of a person, including hands and face, to control a humanoid robot is inaccurate when body parts are estimated one after another because each step passes its errors to the next.
ICRARobots with Attitude: Singularity-Free Quaternion-Based Model-Predictive Control for Agile Legged RobotsCommon ways to describe a robot's rotation using three angles (Euler angles) break down mathematically at certain orientations, causing control errors during fast or large movements.
ICRASimultaneous Collision Detection and Force Estimation for Dynamic Quadrupedal LocomotionFour-legged robots have no single method that can detect bumps and measure how hard they were hit using only joint position sensors, without needing separate tuning for each gait.
IROSExplosive Jumping with Rigid and Articulated Soft Quadrupeds via Example Guided Reinforcement LearningTeaching a four-legged robot to jump well with reinforcement learning is hard because the reward for a good jump is rare, so the learning algorithm has little to work with at the start.
IROSInstantaneous Walkability Determination Method for Almost Linear Passive Dynamic Walker with Nontrivial Limit Cycle StabilityChecking whether a passive walking robot will keep walking stably requires running a slow step-by-step simulation of its full nonlinear motion, which takes too long for quick design checks.
IROSTwo-stage Learning Framework Combining Joint-level Reinforcement Learning and Muscle-level Adaptation for Musculoskeletal LocomotionBodies with many muscles controlling each joint are hard to teach to walk steadily and efficiently because there are too many ways to move the muscles for the same joint motion.
IROSStepping Locomotion for a Walking Excavator Robot using Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning and Action MaskingTeaching a walking excavator to step over obstacles, up steps, and across gaps is complicated, and previous solutions were hard to build and gave no easy way to add human knowledge about what moves are allowed.
IROSMinimizing Acoustic Noise: Enhancing Quiet Locomotion for Quadruped Robots in Indoor ApplicationsFour-legged robots make too much noise when walking indoors, which rules them out for quiet places like hospitals.
IROSComputational Design of Closed Linkages For Robotic LimbsDesigning robot legs that are both light and strong requires searching through many possible link arrangements and sizes at the same time, which is too large a space to do by hand.
IROSLearning Flow-Adaptive Dynamic Model for Robotic Fish Swimming in Unknown Background FlowA robotic fish cannot swim accurately in unknown water currents because its motion model was built without those currents, and measuring the current directly is impractical.
IROSBeware of the Tablet: A Dominant Distractor in Human-Robot InteractionDesigners of human-robot systems don't have clear data on how much a tablet, spoken words, or hand gestures pull a person's attention away from the main task, making it hard to decide which mix of channels to use.
IROSTracking Highly Dynamic Humanoid Motion with Dynamic IMU Measurement FusionWearable motion sensors (IMUs) estimate orientation by treating gravity as a fixed reference, but during fast movement gravity is swamped by other accelerations, so estimates go wrong.
IROSStabilizing Humanoid Robot Trajectory Generation via Physics-Informed Learning and Control-Informed SteeringWhen a humanoid robot learns to move by copying human motion data, its generated movements often violate physical rules — feet slide when they should be planted, and the robot drifts off course over time.
IROSDecARt Leg: Design and Evaluation of a Novel Humanoid Robot Leg with Decoupled Actuation for Agile LocomotionStandard humanoid robot legs have joint motors that fight each other because of how they're connected, which slows down leg swing and limits how fast or agile the robot can move.
IROSTransformable Modular Robots: A CPG-Based Approach to Independent and Collective LocomotionRobots made of separate plug-together modules need a control system that lets each module move on its own but also coordinate smoothly when they connect together into a larger robot.
IROSAn Online Terrain Classification Framework for Legged Robots Based on Fusion of Proprioceptive and Exteroceptive SensorsA legged robot's internal sensors (joint forces and angles) cannot identify surface type, while its cameras and lidar are easily confused by lighting or clutter, so neither alone classifies terrain reliably.
IROSSEM-RRT*: Fast Risk Assessment and Path Planning in Uneven Terrain using Statistical Elevation MapPlanning safe paths for off-road robots over rough ground is slow because dense 3D maps are expensive to process and existing risk scores don't cover all directions efficiently.
IROSSteering Elongate Multi-legged Robots by Modulating Body Undulation WavesLong multi-legged robots can crawl forward well, but there is no clear method for making them turn and follow a curved path reliably.
IROSAddressing Dimensional Scaling in Reinforcement Learning for Symbolic Locomotion Policies through Leveraging Inductive PriorsLearning movement rules for robots with many legs — say 128 — is too slow and fragile with current methods that check every joint one at a time and depend on a pre-trained neural network to get started.
IROSShaken, Not Stirred: A Novel Dataset for Visual Understanding of Glasses in Human-Robot Bartending TasksOff-the-shelf object detectors cannot reliably tell one type of drinking glass from another because glass surfaces are transparent and reflective, causing errors when a robot tries to pour or pick them up.
IROSGeneralized Locomotion in Out-of-distribution Conditions with Robust TransformerA legged robot trained to walk in a fixed set of conditions stumbles when the ground or sensors are different from anything it saw in training.
IROSCo-Adaptation of Embodiment and Control with Self-Imitation Learning ↗Designing a robot's body shape and its control policy together requires a lot of trial-and-error because every time the body changes, the controller has to relearn almost from scratch.
IROSEfficient Learning of A Unified Policy For Whole-body Manipulation and Locomotion SkillsTraining a four-legged robot with a robot arm to walk and use the arm at the same time is hard because standard reinforcement learning gets stuck in poor solutions due to the huge number of things it has to control at once.
IROSLearning-Based Quadruped Robot Framework for Locomotion on Dynamic Rigid PlatformsFour-legged robots trained on firm, steady ground fall over or wander off course when placed on platforms that rock and tilt in all directions, like a ship deck.
IROSWhole-Body Stabilization of Wheeled Bipedal Robots via Decoupled Control of Wheels and LegsRobots with both wheels and legs are hard to keep stable and move quickly because the math tying the wheels and legs together is complicated to control all at once.
IROSRobust and Expressive Humanoid Motion Retargeting via Optimization-Based Rig UnificationTaking motion data recorded on one body shape and making it work correctly on a very different robot body — while keeping the motion looking good and being physically possible — has not been solved at scale.
IROSLearning Whole-Body Control for Small-Sized Quadruped Robots with a Flexible SpineSmall four-legged robots move poorly in tight spaces because their spine and legs are controlled separately rather than together.
IROSTeacher Motion Priors: Enhancing Robot Locomotion over Challenging TerrainA humanoid robot trained with full terrain knowledge (teacher policy) loses performance when switched to a version that only uses its own body sensors (student policy), because the two policies learn to move in different ways.
IROSSteady-State Drifting Equilibrium Analysis of Single-Track Two-Wheeled Robots for Controller DesignNo one had worked out the physics of controlled drifting for single-track two-wheeled robots like bicycles or motorcycles, so there was no principled way to design a drifting controller for them.
IROSRelative Tilt Suppression of a Carried Object Using Base Link Angle Adjustment on a Quadruped-Wheeled RobotA robot that uses both legs and wheels while carrying an object on its back causes the object to tilt as it moves, which can make it fall off.
IROSAdaptive Invariant Extended Kalman Filter for Legged Robot State EstimationLegged robots need to know their body position and speed accurately, but foot slips cause the position tracker to drift or crash, and simply ignoring slipping feet throws away useful information.
IROSTrajectory Generation for Humanoid Backflips and Jumps Based on Whole-Body Dynamics Optimization with Consideration of KKT Residual ConvergenceComputing full-body motion paths for acrobatic moves like backflips fails to converge to a valid solution because the physics equations are highly nonlinear and very sensitive to starting conditions.
IROSAchieving Precise and Reliable Locomotion with Differentiable Simulation-Based System IdentificationTwo-legged robots drift off course because the physical properties used in their simulation, such as mass and friction, do not exactly match the real robot, and correcting those properties normally requires direct torque sensors that many robots lack.
IROSAssistive Guidance System Based on Online Path Structure Recognition for the Visually ImpairedBlind people cannot use robot helpers for walking because the robot needs a pre-built map and cannot understand simple spoken directions.
IROSBio-Inspired Plastic Neural Networks for Zero-Shot Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Complex Animal-Inspired RobotsNeural network controllers for multi-legged robots break down when the robot faces terrain or damage it never encountered during training.
IROSHybrid Data-Driven Predictive Control for Robust and Reactive Exoskeleton Locomotion SynthesisAn exoskeleton must decide where to place its feet and how to move its joints at the same time, in real time, as the ground changes — current controllers treat these as separate problems.
IROSWhole-Body Impedance Control of a Humanoid Robot Based on Human-Human Demonstration for Human-Robot CollaborationA humanoid robot working side by side with a person needs to feel compliant — not stiff — in the right way, but matching its stiffness to the human's in real time is difficult.
IROSCockroach's Turning Strategy Enhanced Hexapod Robot with Flexible TorsoSix-legged robots turn in wide arcs because they only change how their legs step, without bending their body the way insects do.
IROSFlipWalker: Jacob's Ladder toy-inspired robot for locomotion across diverse, complex terrainWheeled robots and most legged robots get stuck on rough outdoor terrain like rocks, snow, and thick grass.
IROSEnv-Mani: Quadrupedal Robot Loco-Manipulation with Environment-in-the-LoopA four-legged robot can't reach things that are outside its normal arm reach because it doesn't use nearby walls or ledges the way a person would lean on a surface to stretch further.
IROSDesign and Active Stability Control of a Wheel-foot Mobile Platform with High TrafficabilityWheeled robots struggle to get over obstacles and legged robots drain their batteries quickly and tip over when carrying heavy loads.
IROSiWalker: Imperative Visual Planning for Walking Humanoid RobotHumanoid walking systems built from separate sensing, planning, and balancing modules pile up errors at each hand-off, making it hard to walk reliably using only camera input.
IROSPerformance consequences of information-based centralization arising from neural and mechanical coupling in a walking robotIt is unclear how the stiffness of a walking robot's joints and how much its leg controllers talk to each other jointly affect how well it walks, because no one has measured both at the same time.
IROSPhysics-informed Neural Motion Planning via Domain Decomposition in Large EnvironmentsNeural path planners that solve a wave-propagation equation (Eikonal PDE) to find the shortest path struggle in large spaces because they have trouble learning fine details and fail to connect distant parts of the map consistently.
IROSLearning Natural and Robust Hexapod Locomotion over Complex Terrains via Motion Priors based on Deep Reinforcement LearningTeaching a six-legged robot to walk using trial-and-error learning produces awkward, jerky gaits and doesn't hold up well on uneven ground.
IROSUnified Locomotion Transformer with Simultaneous Sim-to-Real Transfer for QuadrupedsTeaching a four-legged robot to walk using a teacher-then-student training process requires multiple slow training stages.
IROSLandmark-Based Goal Recognition for Shared Autonomy: A Framework for Enhanced TeleoperationHaving a robot help a human operator by guessing what they are trying to do is usually expensive to compute and requires pre-programmed knowledge about the task.
IROSDiffusion Policies with Value-Conditional Optimization for Offline Reinforcement LearningWhen training a robot policy from a fixed dataset using diffusion models, the model copies bad actions just as faithfully as good ones, making the policy too cautious.
IROSLSTM-MHSA-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning for Accurate Gait Control in Human Musculoskeletal ModelControlling a detailed computer model of the human body with many muscles at once to produce realistic walking and running is too complex for a standard reinforcement learning algorithm.
IROSOptimal Control of Walkers with Parallel Actuation ↗Legged robots with linked leg joints cannot generate good walking motions because existing methods ignore the physical constraints of those linked joints.
IROSImprobability Roller-2: A Hybrid Mobile Robot with Variable Diameter Transformable WheelsWheeled robots with fixed-size wheels cannot adjust their grip and clearance to suit different surfaces like gravel, snow, or steps.
IROSDevelopment of a Cleaning Robot Capable of Self-Propelled Cleaning for Ducts in Real-World Environments Employing a Planetary Gear MechanismGrease builds up inside long kitchen ventilation ducts and cannot be removed by hand or by existing short-range robots because there is no way to push a cleaning tool far enough.
IROSConfidence-Controlled Exploration: Efficient Sparse-Reward Policy Learning for Robot NavigationRobots learning to navigate waste time trying moves that probably won't work because they explore the same way whether they're sure or confused.
IROSSimultaneous Locomotion Mode Classification and Continuous Gait Phase Estimation for Transtibial ProsthesesRobot legs and prosthetics need to know what kind of walking is happening right now and where in the step cycle they are, but doing both together is slow and complicated.
IROSPreferenced Oracle Guided Multi-mode Policies for Dynamic Bipedal Loco-ManipulationTeaching a humanoid robot to both run and kick a ball (or push a box) means it needs to switch between different behaviors like running, slowing down, and kicking, but training separate behaviors for each action doesn't work because they're connected.
IROSOptimal Trajectory Planning in a Vertically Undulating Snake Locomotion using Contact-implicit OptimizationPlanning how a snake should move up a wall is hard because you have to keep track of which body segments touch the ground—too detailed to plan by hand, but too complex for simple methods.
IROSMulti-Objective Optimization of Humanoid Robot Hardware and Control for Multiple Tasks via Genetic AlgorithmsDesigning the body shape and control code of a humanoid robot to do multiple things well is too complex—changing one thing breaks another, and there's no single best answer.
IROSEnergy-Efficient Motion Planner for Legged RobotsRobots that learn to run fast use way too much energy compared to robots designed to walk like animals do.
IROSBridge the Gap: Enhancing Quadruped Locomotion with Vertical Ground PerturbationsFour-legged robots can't walk reliably on bouncy surfaces like bridges that move up and down.
IROSDevelopment of Variable Chain Motor with Shape and Speed-Torque Characteristics Variability and Its Application to a HumanoidHumanoid robots with thin arms can't fit powerful motors that can do both fast and forceful movements.
IROSHeStIa: Asynchronous Embodied Dynamic Locomotion Learning for Walking Robots through Multimodal Large Language ModelsWalking robot controllers do not understand what the movement looks like or what words describe it, so they cannot reason about posture and balance from images and language.
IROSA Novel Effective Loop Gait and Stabilizing Morphology Parameterization in Snake RobotsSnake robot gaits without wheels are too slow and wasteful of energy.
IROSDCM Modulation: A Three-Axis Rotation Stabilization Technique for Bipedal Locomotion ControlWalking robots can't stay balanced when turning or tipping side to side, and existing methods don't handle all three types of rotation smoothly.
IROSLLM-Driven Hierarchical Planning: Long-horizon Task Allocation for Multi-Robot Systems in Cross-Regional EnvironmentsTeams of robots doing big complex tasks across wide areas need to understand instructions and split work between robots, which current systems can't do well together.
IROSIntegrating Trajectory Optimization and Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Jumping with Terrain-Adaptive LandingLegged robots can jump on flat ground but crash on rough or tilted ground after takeoff.
IROSThruster-Enhanced Locomotion: A Decoupled Model Predictive Control with Learned Contact ResidualsA four-legged robot with jet thrusters can't follow one control plan because the leg actuators are too slow to be told what position to hold.
IROSReward Training Wheels: Adaptive Auxiliary Rewards for Robotics Reinforcement LearningHand-tuned bonus rewards for robot learning are fixed and need endless tweaking by experts as the robot gets better at its job.
IROSGACL: Grounded Adaptive Curriculum Learning with Active Task and Performance MonitoringAutomated curriculum learning for complex robot tasks either drifts away from real-world goals or fails to adjust difficulty as the robot's skills improve.
IROSU-Snake: A Small-Sized Smart Underwater Snake RobotUnderwater snake robots are heavy and expensive, and they can't follow curvy paths with changing bend angles well.
IROSLifelong Morphology Learning for Deformable Embodied AgentsSoft robots that reshape their body for different ground types forget how to work on old ground types after learning new ones.
IROSDistributional Decision Transformer: Risk-Sensitive Offline RL via Quantile-Based Critics and Stochastic ReturnWhen learning from stored data, models collapse into one boring plan instead of finding lots of good plans.
IROSLoopSR: Looping Sim-and-Real for Lifelong Policy Adaptation of Legged RobotsRobots trained in simulation don't work well in the real outdoor environment because training made them too general, and they get stuck after being deployed.
IROSUniLegs: Universal Multi-Legged Robot Control through Morphology-Agnostic Policy DistillationDifferent legged robots need different control code, so each new shape requires retraining from scratch.
IROSAdaptive Step Duration for Accurate Foot Placement: Achieving Robust Bipedal Locomotion on Terrains with Restricted FootholdsA two-legged robot can't cross a line of stepping stones using standard planning—there's no path because the feet land too far apart.
IROSAnalysis of Compliant Torso Vibration on Passive Quadruped WalkersA four-legged walking robot's bouncing torso affects how well it walks, but the math for that is messy and hard to understand.
IROSMRS-CWC: A Weakly Constrained Multi-Robot System with Controllable Constraint Stiffness for Mobility and Navigation in Unknown 3D Rough EnvironmentsA team of robots linked together can't cross super-rough ground because either the links are too stiff (hard to steer) or too loose (can't climb).
IROSBiomechanically-Inspired Bipedal Robot Locomotion via Hybrid Gait Representation and Model-Guided Reinforcement LearningA two-legged robot walks stiffly and unevenly at different speeds—it's not smooth like real animals.
IROSReinforcement Learning-based Optimization of Humanoid Joint Motion Control via Text-driven Human Motion MappingHuman motions made by text can't be directly given to a robot because human bodies and robot bodies have different joints and limits.
IROSVibration-Aware Trajectory Optimization for Mobile Robots in Wild Environments via Physics-Informed Neural NetworkPath plans for off-road robots ignore how the wheels bounce and jiggle on rough ground, so the planned paths cause dangerous shaking.
IROSA Novel Terrain Classification System with Planar ECT SensorMobile robots can't reliably tell what ground they're on using cameras or gyros alone because lighting changes and bouncing mess up the readings.
IROSEnhancing the Flexibility of a Quadruped Robot with a 2-DOF Active Spine Using Nonlinear Model Predictive ControlFour-legged robots with stiff spines cannot turn tightly or move agilely like real animals that bend their spine.
IROSEnergy-Efficient Omnidirectional Locomotion for Wheeled Quadrupeds via Predictive Energy-Aware Nominal Gait Selection ↗Four-legged robots with wheels waste power because they walk the same way on every surface and in every direction, even when different walking patterns would use less energy.
IROSAnyBipe: An Automated End-to-End Framework for Training and Deploying Bipedal Robots Powered by Large Language ModelsTeaching two-legged robots to walk takes many steps—writing the learning goals, training the system, checking if it works, then moving it to a real robot—and each step needs human experts.
IROSMysteric-Net: MIMO Hysteretic Friction-aware Lagrangian-based Network for Legged RobotPredicting how a four-legged robot moves is hard because friction depends on history and the legs push against each other in complex ways.
IROSLearning Distributed End-to-End Hunting Locomotion for Multiple Quadruped RobotsTeaching a group of four-legged robots to hunt together requires learning both how to walk steadily and how to chase as a team, without a central control.

Planning motion in real time 115 papers

The problem

Working out the best possible way to move a complex body, moment by moment, is too slow to do properly in real time, especially under wind or other disturbances, and the fast shortcuts give jittery, low-quality results.

The approaches

Instead of solving the hard math exactly, try many possible short-future motions, score each one, and blend the good ones (sampling-based control); learn a rough model of how the body responds so those guesses are better; and add corrections that shrug off outside disturbances.

How it solves it

Trying and scoring many options is fast enough to run live, and the learned model plus disturbance correction makes the guesses good enough to act on.

Handling things by feel, not just by looking 112 papers

The problem

Robot controllers that only track position fail whenever force matters, such as pushing a peg into a hole, peeling a vegetable, wiping, or fitting parts together, because those jobs cannot be done by eye alone.

The approaches

Make force, softness, and touch into signals the controller directly reads and manages, add cheap touch sensors to hands, blend touch with vision, and let the robot decide how firm or gentle to be from moment to moment (compliance).

How it solves it

Once the robot senses and controls force, it can do the contact-heavy jobs that pure position control cannot.

One flexible tool for both seeing and acting 12 papers

The problem

Robots often face several equally good options at once, and simpler methods either freeze up or pick a shaky average of them, giving jerky or unreliable behavior.

The approaches

Reuse a method first built to make images, which starts from random noise and cleans it up into a good result (diffusion), and point it instead at making robot movements and control choices. Newer versions read 3D directly and run faster so they fit on the robot.

How it solves it

It keeps many valid choices cleanly separate instead of collapsing them into one average, giving smoother behavior and a built-in sense of confidence.

Grasping and dexterous hands 242 papers

The problem

Robots struggle to grab objects they have never seen, in cluttered piles, and to pick the right grasp for the job, while the multi-fingered hands that could do fine work are often too expensive, fragile, or hard to maintain.

The approaches

Reason about what an object is for and how it should be grasped, using large AI models; handle open-ended requests in clutter; add cheap plug-and-play touch skin; and build low-cost, reliable multi-fingered hands.

How it solves it

Reasoning about purpose picks a grasp that actually serves the task, and cheaper, tougher hands make fine grasping usable outside the lab.

ICRA7cViViDex: Learning Vision-Based Dexterous Manipulation from Human VideosTeaching a multi-fingered robot hand from human video is hard because the hand-tracking estimates are noisy and the robot has no access to exact object positions when it runs in the real world.

ICRA6cGraspSAM: When Segment Anything Model Meets Grasp DetectionGrasp detection systems trained on limited data struggle to generalize to new object types and cannot easily take user input such as pointing at an object or naming it.
ICRA6cRL-GSBridge: 3D Gaussian Splatting Based Real2Sim2Real Method for Robotic Manipulation LearningTraining a robot arm in simulation and then using it in the real world fails because the simulated images look too different from reality.
ICRA6cCatch It! Learning to Catch in Flight with Mobile Dexterous HandsCatching a thrown object with a robot that has a moving base, an arm, and a multi-fingered hand is extremely hard because the whole body must coordinate in a fraction of a second across many kinds of objects.
ICRA5cGeneral-Purpose Clothes Manipulation with Semantic KeypointsRobots cannot handle many different types of clothing or tasks such as folding, hanging, or placing garments, because fabric changes shape in too many ways.
ICRA5cRobot Utility Models: General Policies for Zero-Shot Deployment in New EnvironmentsRobot manipulation skills trained in one place stop working when the robot is moved to a new environment, requiring expensive retraining each time.
ICRA5cDa-Vil: Adaptive Dual-Arm Manipulation with Reinforcement Learning and Variable Impedance ControlA two-armed robot handling large or heavy objects needs to constantly adjust how stiff or compliant its arms are, and getting that right for objects of many different shapes and masses is hard to do by hand.
ICRA5c$\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{R}, \mathcal{O})$ Grasp: A Unified Representation of Robot and Object Interaction for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous GraspingTeaching a multi-fingered robot hand to grasp objects requires retraining from scratch each time the hand has a different shape, which is slow and expensive.
IROS5cAffordGrasp: In-Context Affordance Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Task-Oriented Grasping in ClutterRobots can't pick up new objects or work well when things are messy unless they've been trained on that exact task.
ICRA4cVegetable Peeling: A Case Study in Constrained Dexterous ManipulationRobot hands that can reorient objects in their fingers don't naturally end up holding the object in the right grip for a follow-up task like peeling.
ICRA4cActive Vision Might Be All You Need: Exploring Active Vision in Bimanual Robotic ManipulationWhen a robot uses fixed cameras, parts of a task can be blocked from view or cut off, which makes it fail more often.
ICRA4cThe Ingredients for Robotic Diffusion TransformersIt is unclear which design choices matter when building a robot policy that uses a large Transformer combined with a diffusion process to generate actions, so practitioners have little guidance.
ICRA4cSelf-Improving Autonomous Underwater ManipulationUnderwater robots struggle to act on their own because water currents and murky conditions are hard to model, so most systems still need a human in the loop.
ICRA4cIs Linear Feedback on Smoothed Dynamics Sufficient for Stabilizing Contact-Rich Plans?Robot plans that involve many contacts — like pushing or sliding objects — are hard to keep stable during execution because contacts cause sudden changes that break the assumptions of standard feedback controllers.
ICRA4cTask-Oriented 6-DoF Grasp Pose Detection in CluttersRobots need to pick up objects differently depending on what they will do with them next (e.g., hand a knife by the handle vs. use it to cut), but no dataset or method existed to solve this in a messy pile of objects.
ICRA3cBridging the Human to Robot Dexterity Gap Through Object-Oriented RewardsTeaching a multi-fingered robot hand to do fine tasks by watching human videos doesn't work directly because the robot hand looks and moves very differently from a human hand.
ICRA3cDROP: Dexterous Reorientation via Online PlanningReorienting an object held in a robot hand requires precise coordinated finger movements, which usually demands long and costly training runs in simulation.
ICRA3cDA-Fusion: Deformable Attention-Based RGB-D Fusion Transformer for Unseen Object Instance Segmentation ↗Picking objects out of a cluttered bin is unreliable when a robot uses only color images or only depth images, because each alone misses details the other would catch.
ICRA3cvMF-Contact: Uncertainty-Aware Evidential Learning for Probabilistic Contact-Grasp in Noisy ClutterDetecting good grasp points in messy, noisy scenes is hard, and current methods cannot tell the difference between uncertainty caused by sensor noise and uncertainty caused by seeing a completely new object type.
ICRA3cTransDiff: Diffusion-Based Method for Manipulating Transparent Objects Using a Single RGB-D ImageDepth sensors cannot measure the distance to transparent objects accurately because light passes through or reflects off them, so robots cannot figure out where to grasp them.
ICRA3cIn the Wild Ungraspable Object Picking with Bimanual Nonprehensile ManipulationSome grocery items are too large, heavy, or awkwardly shaped for a robot to pick up with a single suction cup or parallel-jaw gripper from a packed shelf.
ICRA3cUniAff: A Unified Representation of Affordances for Tool Usage and Articulation with Vision-Language ModelsRobots handle tools and jointed objects (like drawers or scissors) using separate, incompatible systems, so there is no single way to describe what part of an object to touch and how to move it.
ICRA3cScaling Diffusion Policy in Transformer to 1 Billion Parameters for Robotic ManipulationMaking robot imitation-learning models larger by adding transformer layers causes training to become unstable, so the accuracy gains expected from bigger models do not appear.
IROS3cPhyGrasp: Generalizing Robotic Grasping with Physics-informed Large Multimodal ModelsRobot grasping models fail on uncommon objects because they do not reason about material properties like weight distribution or slipperiness, only shape.
IROS3cManiGaussian++: General Robotic Bimanual Manipulation with Hierarchical Gaussian World ModelWhen a robot uses two arms together to handle an object, models trained on single-arm work can't predict what happens because they ignore how the helper arm affects things.
ICRA2cPUGS: Perceptual Uncertainty for Grasp Selection in Underwater EnvironmentsUnderwater 3D scans are noisy and incomplete, so a robot picking objects underwater may try to grab based on bad geometry and fail.
ICRA2cBiFold: Bimanual Cloth Folding with Language Guidance ↗Folding clothes with two robot arms following a spoken instruction is hard because cloth changes shape unpredictably and different garments look very different.
ICRA2cDemoStart: Demonstration-Led Auto-Curriculum Applied to Sim-to-Real with Multi-Fingered RobotsTeaching a three-fingered robot hand complex tasks through trial-and-error in simulation takes an enormous number of attempts because success is rare when starting from random positions.
ICRA2cImplicit Articulated Robot Morphology Modeling with Configuration Space Neural Signed Distance Functions ↗Motion planners need to know quickly and accurately how far any part of the robot is from an obstacle, but existing approaches are either slow or not accurate enough.
ICRA2cBODex: Scalable and Efficient Robotic Dexterous Grasp Synthesis Using Bilevel OptimizationCreating large sets of valid multi-finger grasps for training robot hands is slow and the math used to enforce physical contact rules is hard to run at scale.
ICRA2cAdaptive Grasping of Moving Objects in Dense Clutter via Global-to-Local Detection and Static-to-Dynamic PlanningGrabbing an object that is both moving and surrounded by other objects is hard because you have to track it accurately and plan a grasp fast enough to catch it.
ICRA2cReVLA: Reverting Visual Domain Limitation of Robotic Foundation ModelsWhen a general vision-language-action model is fine-tuned on robot task data, it loses its ability to handle unfamiliar visual conditions such as new lighting or backgrounds.
ICRA2cBlox-Net: Generative Design-for-Robot-Assembly Using VLM Supervision, Physics Simulation, and a Robot with ResetGenerating a block structure that both looks like a named concept and can actually be assembled by a robot arm — without a human checking each design — is an unsolved end-to-end problem.
ICRA2cYou Only Estimate Once: Unified, One-stage, Real-Time Category-Level Articulated Object 6D Pose Estimation for Robotic GraspingFiguring out the exact position and joint angles of objects like scissors or drawers from a 3D scan currently requires running several separate programs in sequence, which is too slow for a robot acting in real time.
ICRA2cQdgset: a Large Scale Grasping Dataset Generated With Quality-DiversityBuilding large, varied collections of robot grasp data is slow because simple search methods waste many attempts before finding grasps that actually work on a given object.
ICRA2cTranSplat: Surface Embedding-Guided 3D Gaussian Splatting for Transparent Object ManipulationDepth sensors fail on transparent objects because light bends and reflects in ways that break the assumptions those sensors rely on, so the robot cannot tell where the object really is.
ICRA2cDART: Dexterous Augmented Reality Teleoperation Platform for Large-Scale Robot Data Collection in SimulationCollecting the large amounts of dexterous robot manipulation data needed to train good policies is slow and tiring when operators must work with physical robots that break down and need constant resetting.
ICRA2cQuickGrasp: Lightweight Antipodal Grasp Planning with Point CloudsMethods for figuring out where a robot hand should grab an object are often slow, produce different answers each run, and fail on objects they were not trained on.
ICRA2cComposing Dextrous Grasping and In-Hand Manipulation via Scoring with a Reinforcement Learning Critic ↗A hand that can reposition an object in its fingers still needs to start with a grip that makes that repositioning possible, and choosing that starting grip automatically is an unsolved problem.
ICRA2cHierarchical Contact-Rich Trajectory Optimization for Multi-Modal Manipulation Using Tight Convex Relaxations ↗Planning a robot's full motion path together with deciding which contacts to make and when is too slow to solve as one problem because the number of possible contact sequences grows too large.
ICRA2cPUGS: Zero-Shot Physical Understanding with Gaussian SplattingRobots cannot tell how heavy, slippery, or hard an object is just by looking at it, which makes it hard to pick up new objects correctly.
ICRA2cKALIE: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language Models for Open-World Manipulation Without Robot DataGetting a robot to pick up and interact with objects it has never seen before normally requires collecting a large amount of data using the actual robot, which is expensive.
ICRA2cTowards Autonomous Wood-Log Grasping with a Forestry Crane: Simulator and BenchmarkingA forestry crane needs to pick up heavy logs of different sizes on its own, but the crane's motion is hard to control because its joints interact in complex ways.
ICRA2cOne-Shot Dual-Arm Imitation LearningA two-armed robot cannot reliably learn a precise coordinated task from just one human demonstration without needing extra data or retraining.
ICRA2cDiscrete Policy: Learning Disentangled Action Space for Multi-Task Robotic ManipulationWhen a single robot policy must handle many different tasks, the range of possible actions it needs to cover grows so large and mixed that the policy becomes inaccurate.
IROS2cFSGlove: An Inertial-Based Hand Tracking System with Shape-Aware CalibrationExisting motion-capture gloves track too few hand joints and ignore that each person's hand is a different size and shape, which limits their use in tasks that need precise finger control.
IROS2cRoboDexVLM: Visual Language Model-Enabled Task Planning and Motion Control for Dexterous Robot ManipulationRobots with multi-fingered hands cannot yet plan long sequences of varied tasks using open-ended language instructions while also figuring out how to grasp unfamiliar objects.
IROS2cAdapting Pre-Trained Vision Models for Novel Instance Detection and SegmentationRecognizing and outlining specific objects in images is hard when the objects appear at many angles and the system has only a few example images to learn from.
IROS2cHelpful DoggyBot: Open-World Object Fetching using Legged Robots and Vision-Language ModelsFour-legged robots have no arms, don't understand what they see, and can't walk well enough indoors to fetch things people ask for.
IROS2cContactDexNet: Multi-fingered Robotic Hand Grasping in Cluttered Environments through Hand-Object Contact Semantic MappingA five-fingered robot hand can't grasp well in crowded bins because it doesn't know where to touch the object or how to avoid bumping things.
ICRA1cLearning Coordinated Bimanual Manipulation Policies Using State Diffusion and Inverse Dynamics ModelsTeaching a robot to use both arms together is hard because standard learning methods do not separately handle predicting how things will move and figuring out which arm actions cause those movements.
ICRA1cZeroBP: Learning Position-Aware Correspondence for Zero-Shot 6D Pose Estimation in Bin-PickingFinding the exact position and angle of textureless parts piled in a bin is hard because similar-looking regions on the part produce confusing matches when using only local appearance.
ICRA1cGAPartManip: A Large-Scale Part-Centric Dataset for Material-Agnostic Articulated Object ManipulationRobot arms fail to interact with hinged or sliding objects like doors and drawers when the surfaces are transparent or shiny, because depth cameras cannot read those materials well.
ICRA1cNeuGrasp: Generalizable Neural Surface Reconstruction with Background Priors for Material-Agnostic Object Grasp DetectionRobots cannot reliably grasp transparent or shiny objects because depth cameras give bad or missing readings on those surfaces.
ICRA1cHighly Dynamic Physical Interaction for Robotics: Design and Control of an Active Remote Center of ComplianceRobot arms are either springy and safe to touch but slow, or stiff and fast but too rigid for delicate contact tasks like pushing a peg into a tight hole.
ICRA1cMuST: Multi-Head Skill Transformer for Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation with Skill ProgressRobots have trouble learning a sequence of distinct hand motions — like pick, orient, and pack — and knowing when to switch from one to the next.
ICRA1cDexterous Ungrasping Manipulation in Three DimensionsRobots do not have reliable ways to carefully set down thin or slender objects by rolling or sliding them out of a grip in three dimensions without dropping or misplacing them.
ICRA1cIntegrating Active Sensing and Rearrangement Planning for Efficient Object Retrieval from Unknown, Confined, Cluttered EnvironmentsRetrieving a specific object from a packed, enclosed space is hard because the robot must figure out both where to look next and which blocking objects to move, and previous work handled those two problems separately.
ICRA1cEfficient 7-DoF Grasp for Target-Driven Object in Dense Cluttered ScenesWhen a robot needs to grab a specific object from a crowded pile, figuring out exactly where and how to grip it — including the width of the hand — in real time from a single camera view is slow and error-prone.
ICRA1cOcclusion-Aware 6D Pose Estimation with Depth-Guided Graph Encoding and Cross-Semantic Fusion for Robotic GraspingFiguring out the exact position and orientation of a partially hidden object is hard because standard networks treat each visible surface point in isolation and miss how points relate to each other.
ICRA1cOne-Shot Manipulation Strategy Learning by Making Contact AnalogiesTeaching a robot how to handle a new object by showing it just one example on a different object is hard because the robot must figure out where to touch the new object despite different shapes and sizes.
ICRA1cSampling-Based Grasp and Collision Prediction for Assisted TeleoperationWhen a human remotely controls a robot, helping it avoid collisions and grasp objects safely in real time is too slow if solved as a full math optimization each step.
ICRA1cSafety and Naturalness Perceptions of Robot-to-Human Handovers Performed by Data-Driven Robotic Mimicry of Human GiversIt is unclear whether making a robot copy the way a human holds and hands over objects makes the handover feel safer and more natural, especially across many different objects.
ICRA1cRoboCrowd: Scaling Robot Data Collection Through CrowdsourcingGathering enough robot demonstration data for imitation learning is slow because it depends on a small pool of trained operators.
ICRA1cRobotic-CLIP: Fine-Tuning CLIP on Action Data for Robotic ApplicationsA popular vision-language model (CLIP) was trained only on still photos with captions, so it does not understand actions or motion — limiting its use for robots that need to act.
ICRA1cMulti-Heuristic Robotic Bin Packing of Regular and Irregular ObjectsPacking oddly shaped products into boxes in a warehouse is hard for robots because no single placement rule works well for all shapes and packing rules.
ICRA1cGET-Zero: Graph Embodiment Transformer for Zero-Shot Embodiment GeneralizationA robot policy trained on one hardware body stops working when a joint is removed or a limb length changes, so every hardware change requires expensive retraining.
ICRA1cFrom Simple to Complex Skills: The Case of In-Hand Object ReorientationTeaching a robot hand to rotate objects to any target angle in simulation and then having that work on a real hand takes huge amounts of tuning for each new task.
ICRA1cRM4D: A Combined Reachability and Inverse Reachability Map for Common 6-/7-Axis Robot Arms by Dimensionality Reduction to 4DPrecomputing which positions a robot arm can reach, and from which robot positions a given point in space is reachable, normally requires building two separate large 6D tables that take a long time to compute.
ICRA1cReinforcement Learning with Lie Group Orientations for RoboticsCommon ways to represent 3D rotation (such as Euler angles or quaternions) fed into a learning algorithm do not match the true mathematical structure of rotation, which slows learning and hurts performance.
ICRA1cZeroMimic: Distilling Robotic Manipulation Skills from Web VideosTeaching a robot manipulation skills normally requires collecting robot-specific recordings, which is expensive, even though millions of hours of humans doing the same tasks already exist on video.
ICRA1cUAD: Unsupervised Affordance Distillation for Generalization in Robotic ManipulationTeaching a robot where to grasp or act on objects normally requires a person to label many images by hand, and the result still fails on objects the robot has not seen before.
ICRA1cLearning Dual-Arm Coordination for Grasping Large Flat Objects ↗A single robot arm cannot pick up a large flat object lying on a surface without awkward repositioning, but teaching two arms to coordinate the grasp is hard.
ICRA1cQuadWBG: Generalizable Quadrupedal Whole-Body GraspingA four-legged robot that also has an arm needs to walk to an object and grab it smoothly, but combining stable walking with precise arm control in varied real-world settings is hard.
ICRA1cVariable-Friction In-Hand Manipulation for Arbitrary Objects via Diffusion-Based Imitation LearningRobotic hands that can change grip friction to rotate objects in-hand have only worked on simple shapes with a fixed target orientation, requiring a new control design for every new object.
ICRA1cGAGrasp: Geometric Algebra Diffusion for Dexterous GraspingGenerating stable grasps for a multi-fingered robot hand is hard because the correct grasp changes completely when the object is rotated or moved, and most models have to relearn this from scratch for each pose.
ICRA1cFlat'n'Fold: A Diverse Multi-Modal Dataset for Garment Perception and Manipulation ↗Existing datasets for teaching robots to fold clothes are too small, cover too few garment types, and do not record all the sensor data needed to train a general-purpose folding system.
IROS1cHannesImitation: Grasping with the Hannes Prosthetic Hand via Imitation LearningProsthetic hand controllers are usually hand-coded for specific situations and break down in new settings, but no one had tried teaching a prosthetic hand by showing it examples of grasping.
IROS1cTask-Aware Robotic Grasping by evaluating Quality Diversity Solutions through Foundation ModelsRobot grasping systems focus on not dropping an object but do not think about which part of the object to grab for a specific task, such as picking up a knife by the handle rather than the blade.
IROS1cEnhancing Single Image to 3D Generation using Gaussian Splatting and Hybrid Diffusion PriorsTurning a single photo into a 3D model either gets the shape right but the surface looks blurry, or the surface looks sharp but the shape is wrong.
IROS1cKARL: Kalman-Filter Assisted Reinforcement Learner for Dynamic Object Tracking and GraspingA robot trying to grab a fast-moving object with a wrist-mounted camera loses track whenever the object moves out of the camera's view, breaking the robot's learned control policy.
IROS1cGraphGarment: Learning Garment Dynamics for Bimanual Cloth Manipulation TasksRobots struggle to hang or fold clothes because cloth moves in complicated ways that are hard to predict, and simulated predictions do not match reality.
IROS1cCross-Embodiment Robotic Manipulation Synthesis via Guided Demonstrations through CycleVAE and Human Behavior TransformerTeaching a robot to manipulate objects by watching humans is hard because there are no matched pairs of recordings showing a human and a robot doing the exact same motion.
IROS1cPlayful DoggyBot: Learning Agile and Precise Quadrupedal LocomotionFour-legged robots struggle to move fast and catch or grab objects accurately at the same time, because speed and precision pull against each other.
IROS1cDisentangled Object-Centric Image Representation for Robotic ManipulationWhen a robot learns to pick objects from camera images in a cluttered scene, its visual model mixes up the target object, obstacles, and the robot's own arm, which makes learning harder and the skill less general.
IROS1cHGDiffuser: Efficient Task-Oriented Grasp Generation via Human-Guided Grasp Diffusion ModelsRobots picking objects for a specific task—like handing a knife by the handle—are slow because they first generate thousands of candidate grasps without considering the task, then filter most of them out.
IROS1cOne-Shot Affordance Grounding of Deformable Objects in Egocentric Organizing ScenesRobots struggle to figure out where and how to interact with soft or deformable objects (like cloth or bags) when given only one example, because these objects change shape, look different in different scenes, and language descriptions are often vague.
IROS1cFree-form language-based robotic reasoning and graspingPicking objects from a cluttered bin based on open-ended spoken or written instructions is hard because the robot must understand language and figure out which objects are blocked by others.
IROS1cSimultaneous Pick and Place Detection by Combining SE(3) Diffusion Models with Differential KinematicsGrasp pose generators often produce poses the robot arm physically cannot reach, or that conflict with where the object needs to be placed, requiring slow after-the-fact filtering.
IROS1cLearning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation with Multifingered Hands via Visuomotor DiffusionTeaching a multi-fingered robot hand complex in-hand tasks is hard because collecting good training demonstrations is difficult and a few bad examples can ruin the learned skill.
IROS1cB4P: Simultaneous Grasp and Motion Planning for Object Placement via Parallelized Bidirectional Forests and Path RepairPick-and-place planners that first choose a grasp and then plan the move often get stuck because the chosen grasp has no valid path to the drop-off location in a cluttered space.
IROS1cIntegrating Ergonomics and Manipulability for Upper Limb Postural Optimization in Bimanual Human-Robot CollaborationWhen a person and a robot carry an object together with both hands, there is no method that jointly optimizes how safe the posture is for the person and how much force the person can apply.
IROS1cManiDP: Manipulability-Aware Diffusion Policy for Posture-Dependent Bimanual ManipulationWhen two robot arms work together, the exact posture of the arms matters for tasks that need force or speed in a specific direction, but current learning methods ignore posture when deciding how to move.
IROS1cVAPO: Visibility-Aware Keypoint Localization for Efficient 6DoF Object Pose EstimationWhen parts of an object are hidden or turned away from the camera, the system still tries to use those hidden reference points to figure out the object's position and angle, which gives bad results.
IROS1cPAVLM: Advancing Point Cloud based Affordance Understanding Via Vision-Language ModelAI vision-language models could not reliably identify the exact parts of a 3D object that a robot should grasp or press.
IROS1cOpAC: An Optimization-Augmented Control Framework for Single and Coordinated Multi-Arm Robotic ManipulationSome manipulation tasks need a robot to move freely over long distances while also pressing against surfaces with exactly the right force — and no single control method handles both at once.
IROS1cOmni-Scan: Creating Visually-Accurate Digital Twin Object Models Using a Bimanual Robot with Handover and Gaussian Splat MergingWhen a robot holds an object to scan it, the robot hand blocks the camera view of the part it is gripping, leaving hidden surfaces out of the final 3D model—you can not scan what the gripper hides.
IROS1cVISO-Grasp: Vision-Language Informed Spatial Object-centric 6-DoF Active View Planning and Grasping in Clutter and Invisibility ↗Grasping objects hidden under other stuff is hard when the robot cannot see where to grab and must figure out the best angle to look from.
IROS1cETA-IK: Execution-Time-Aware Inverse Kinematics for Dual-Arm SystemsTwo-armed robot controllers plan joint positions using rough guesses about speed, which leads to slow actual movement.
IROS1cA Multi-modal Hand Imitation Dataset for Dexterous HandRobots copying human hand movements only get color camera data but need richer information like 3D shape and hand pose to learn delicate finger skills.
IROS1cDynamic planning and assembly for constructing mortar-joint multi-leaf stone masonry walls with a robotic armRobots cannot build stone walls with mortar joints because stones are irregular, mortar is wet and unpredictable, and walls need dense packing with live corrections.
IROS1cHierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Articulated Tool Manipulation with Multifingered HandDexterous hands can't grasp tools like tweezers or scissors because the tool's shape changes as it opens and closes, confusing the hand about how to hold it.
IROS1cZero-Shot Peg Insertion: Identifying Mating Holes and Estimating SE(2) Poses with Vision-Language ModelsA robot cannot put a peg in a hole it has never seen before without special training because it does not know where the hole is or how it lines up.
IROS1cA Planning Framework for Stable Robust Multi-Contact ManipulationWhen robots touch something at many points at once, they need to keep all those touches stable and not freak out if sensors are off by a bit.
IROS1cGeometric Retargeting: A Principled, Ultrafast Neural Hand Retargeting AlgorithmWhen a person controls a robot hand by remote, the computer must turn human finger positions into robot finger positions very fast, but this is hard to set up and usually needs hand-labeled examples.
IROS1cSR3D: Unleashing Single-view 3D Reconstruction for Transparent and Specular Object GraspingClear and shiny objects break depth cameras, so robots can't see them to grab them.
ICRARoCoDA: Counterfactual Data Augmentation for Data-Efficient Robot Learning from DemonstrationsA robot trained on a small set of demonstrations often fails when objects are in a new position, a different color, or the scene looks slightly different.
ICRAHigh-Quality Unknown Object Instance Segmentation via Quadruple Boundary Error RefinementWhen a robot looks at a cluttered scene, its first pass at separating one object from another often leaves messy edges—parts are merged together or split apart—which causes the robot to grab incorrectly.
ICRATowards Autonomous Data Annotation and System-Agnostic Robotic Grasping Benchmarking with 3D-Printed FixturesTesting robots that pick up objects requires someone to manually label where every object is in every photo, which is slow and hard to repeat the same way twice.
ICRAVisually Robust Adversarial Imitation Learning from Videos with Contrastive LearningA robot trying to learn from expert videos fails when the video looks different from what the robot's own camera sees — different lighting, background, or color.
ICRATWIN: Two-handed Intelligent Benchmark for Bimanual ManipulationThere is no simulated test set with enough variety of tasks to study whether a robot can coordinate both arms across many different situations.
ICRAHeterogeneous Sensor Fusion and Active Perception for Transparent Object Reconstruction with a PDM2 Sensor and a CameraTransparent objects like glass cups are invisible to standard depth cameras, and the specialized sensors that can detect them are too slow to scan a whole object quickly enough for practical robot use.
ICRANeRF-Based Transparent Object Grasping Enhanced by Shape PriorsCameras and depth sensors cannot see transparent objects properly because light passes through them, so robots misjudge their shape and fail to pick them up.
ICRAMatch Policy: A Simple Pipeline from Point Cloud Registration to Manipulation PoliciesTeaching a robot to pick up and place objects precisely is hard because it needs to infer exact relative positions from only a few demonstrations, which is difficult to learn directly.
ICRAPatch Tree: Exploiting the Gauss Map and Principal Component Analysis for Robotic GraspingA robot gripper needs to figure out where to grab curved everyday objects, which requires understanding small local shapes and overall object shape at the same time, and doing it fast enough to be practical.
ICRAMulti-Layer Feature Exchange Transformer for Multi-View 6D Object Pose Estimation in Robot Bin PickingWhen a robot tries to figure out the exact position and orientation of objects in a bin using multiple cameras, the cameras' information is combined too late in the process, so shiny or hidden objects are often mis-detected.
ICRALearning Dexterous Bimanual Catch Skills Through Adversarial-Cooperative Heterogeneous-Agent Reinforcement LearningTraining two robot hands to catch objects thrown at them is hard because the throw difficulty and the catching skill both need to improve at the same time.
ICRAOptimize and Coordinate Multiple DMPs Under Constraints to Achieve a Collaborative Manipulation Task ↗Getting two robot arms to cooperate on a shared task is hard when each arm's motion was learned separately, because the motions do not naturally stay in sync or meet task rules.
ICRADiffusion-Informed Probabilistic Contact Search for Multi-Finger ManipulationPlanning how a multi-finger robot hand should touch and move an object requires searching through a huge space of possible contact sequences, and learned methods alone are limited by the quality of training data.
ICRAAutonomous Sensor Exchange and Calibration for Cornstalk Nitrate Monitoring RobotA farm robot that measures nitrogen in cornstalks has to have its sensors swapped and re-calibrated by hand, which stops it from running on its own for long periods.
ICRAEfficient Gradient-Based Inference for Manipulation Planning in Contact Factor GraphsPlanning how a robot should touch, push, or grasp an object requires reasoning about many physical rules at once — contact forces, motion, geometry — and doing that quickly is very hard.
ICRALeveraging Semantic and Geometric Information for Zero-Shot Robot-to-Human HandoverWhen a robot hands an object to a person, it must grip the object in a spot that leaves the human's preferred holding area free, which is hard to get right across many different objects.
ICRARobotic Dry-Stacking of Clochái with Irregular StonesRobots could build simple stone walls but not the more complex corbelled dome shelters (clochán) made of irregular natural stones, because those require each stone to overhang the last in a stable way.
ICRAInterface Matters: Comparing First and Third-Person Perspective Interfaces for Bi-Manual Robot Behavioural CloningIt is not known whether operators record better training demonstrations for robot learning when they see the robot's view (first-person) versus an outside observer's view (third-person).
ICRAEfficient Cross-Boundary Grasping in Stacked Clutter with Single-Visual Mapping Multi-StepGrasping objects stacked underwater through a water-air boundary is hard because the water surface distorts the visual feed and the robot must pick objects in the right order to avoid knocking everything over.
ICRAPrompt-Responsive Object Retrieval with Memory-Augmented Student-Teacher LearningA robot needs to pick a specific object from a cluttered scene based on a user's description, but linking what the user says to the precise hand movements needed is an unsolved problem.
ICRASynthesizing Grasps and Regrasps for Complex Manipulation TasksMany manipulation tasks, like rotating an object, require the robot to change its grip partway through, but figuring out when to re-grip and how is hard, especially when the robot can only see part of the object.
ICRAPoint Cloud Decomposition for Task-Oriented GraspingA robot trying to grasp a specific part of an object has no good way to find that graspable region from a 3D point cloud without needing a large labeled dataset or object-specific knowledge.
ICRAHow About Them Apples: 3D Pose and Cluster Estimation of Apple Fruitlets in a Commercial OrchardA robot that thins apple trees — removes some small fruit so the rest grow larger — must find and locate tightly packed tiny fruitlets in 3D in a real orchard, which current systems cannot do reliably.
ICRAOptimizing Robot Programming: Mixed Reality Gripper ControlCommon ways to move a robot end-effector in mixed reality — using thumbsticks or mapping hand motions directly — are slow, error-prone, or mentally tiring.
ICRARobust Optical Transceiver Manipulation in Cluttered Cable Environments Using 3D Scene Understanding and PlanningSwapping small data-center plug-in cards by hand is slow, but doing it with a robot is hard because masses of cables block the view and the path to the card.
ICRAIntelliRMS: A Robotic Manipulation System for Domain-Specific Tasks Using Vision and Language Foundational ModelsGeneral-purpose AI models fail to meet the high accuracy needed for industrial pick-and-place robots that must correctly identify and grab specific items from bins.

Rules across everything

Making training examples cheaper 506 papers

The problem

Teaching robots by showing them what to do needs lots of good examples, and collecting them by hand on real robots is slow and expensive, which is the field's real bottleneck.

The approaches

Better rigs to record a person doing the task, including see-through headset gear, head-worn cameras, and real-time two-handed puppeteering; automatic ways to make many more examples from a few; making large batches of fake data inside a computer; and scanning real objects into computer copies by picking them up.

How it solves it

More and cheaper examples, with less human effort per example, attack the bottleneck head-on.

ICRA4cDTRT: Enhancing Human Intent Estimation and Role Allocation for Physical Human-Robot CollaborationWhen a person and a robot move an object together, the robot struggles to predict what the person plans to do next and to smoothly hand over or take control at the right moment.
ICRA4cUse the Force, Bot! - Force-Aware ProDMP with Event-Based ReplanningStandard movement-primitive methods for teaching robots by demonstration don't account for the forces the robot feels during contact, so they struggle with tasks that require careful pushing or pressing.
ICRA4cHuman-Agent Joint Learning for Efficient Robot Manipulation Skill AcquisitionCollecting enough teleoperated demonstrations to train a manipulation policy is tiring and time-consuming because the operator must stay fully in control the entire time.
ICRA4cArena 4.0: a Comprehensive Ros2 Development and Benchmarking Platform for Human-Centric Navigation Using Generative-Model-Based Environment GenerationTesting social navigation algorithms requires a wide variety of realistic indoor environments with people in them, and creating those environments by hand is slow and does not scale.
ICRA4cHand-Object Interaction Pretraining from VideosTeaching robots to handle objects well requires large amounts of robot-collected data, which is slow and expensive to gather.
IROS4cThe Common Objects Underwater (COU) Dataset for Robust Underwater Object DetectionTraining data for underwater robots mostly covers fish and coral, leaving out the human-made objects — tools, debris, other robots — that a working underwater robot needs to recognize.
ICRA3cAsynchronous Multi-Object Tracking with an Event Camera ↗Tracking many small fast-moving objects like bees is too slow and blurry with standard cameras, and event cameras — which report pixel changes as they happen — have no mature pipeline for tracking many objects at once.
ICRA3cFDPP: Fine-Tune Diffusion Policy with Human PreferenceA robot policy trained by copying recorded demonstrations cannot be adjusted after deployment to match what a specific person actually wants.
ICRA3cIterative Volume Fusion for Asymmetric Stereo MatchingWhen two cameras in a pair have different lenses or resolutions, standard depth-from-stereo methods produce distorted depth estimates because they assume both cameras look identical.
ICRA3cIBURD: Image Blending for Underwater Robotic DetectionTraining a computer to spot trash on the ocean floor is hard because there are very few labeled underwater photos available to learn from.
ICRA3cP3-PO: Prescriptive Point Priors for Visuo-Spatial Generalization of Robot PoliciesRobot policies trained from camera images fail on new objects or messier scenes because the raw pixel view is too sensitive to visual change.
ICRA3cA Dataset and Benchmark for Shape Completion of Fruits for Agricultural RoboticsFruit-picking robots need to estimate the full 3D shape of a fruit even when leaves or other fruits block part of the view, but no public dataset existed to train or test methods for this.
ICRA3cEnhancing AR-to-Robot Registration Accuracy: A Comparative Study of Marker Detection Algorithms and Registration ParametersLining up an augmented-reality display with a real robot's location is sensitive to which marker-detection software and setup you use, but no one had compared them all in the same study.
ICRA3cRT-Affordance: Affordances are Versatile Intermediate Representations for Robot ManipulationRobots trained to pick up and move objects often fail on new tasks because the information they are given — a sentence or a picture of the goal — is either too vague or too specific to transfer well.
ICRA3cBootstrapping Object-Level Planning with Large Language ModelsGetting a robot to plan a new manipulation task in a standard planning language (PDDL) is difficult because large language models often produce goals that are inconsistent or impossible to satisfy.
ICRA3cJoint 3D Point Cloud Segmentation Using Real-Sim Loop: From Panels to Trees and BranchesLabeling 3D scans of orchards at multiple levels — whole rows, individual trees, and individual branches — is expensive and time-consuming, yet a robot needs all three levels to harvest fruit.
ICRA3cCascaded Diffusion Models for Neural Motion PlanningGenerative planners that create motion paths in one step are good at local moves but often produce paths that hit obstacles when the overall route is complicated.
ICRA3cHardware-Accelerated Ray Tracing for Discrete and Continuous Collision Detection on GPUsChecking whether a robot arm will hit an obstacle is slow when the shapes are complex, which limits how fast motion planners can test thousands of candidate paths.
ICRA3cMeshDMP: Motion Planning on Discrete Manifolds Using Dynamic Movement PrimitivesTeaching a robot to polish or sand a curved surface is hard because the shape of each workpiece varies, so a motion learned on one part does not transfer cleanly to a differently shaped part.
ICRA3cPersonalization in Human-Robot Interaction Through Preference-Based Action Representation LearningAdapting a robot's behavior to fit a specific person's preferences using preference feedback requires retraining the whole policy from scratch for each user, wasting everything already learned.
